Head & Neck | Chapter 8

Upper Limb（上肢）

Superficial Veins（淺層靜脈）

Large veins embedded in the superficial fascia of the upper limb are often used to access a patient’s vascular system and to withdraw blood. The most significant of these veins are the cephalic vein、basilic vein、and median cubital vein (Fig. 7.18).

The cephalic and basilic veins originate from the dorsal venous network on the back of the hand.

Cephalic Vein

The cephalic vein originates over the anatomical snuffbox at the base of the thumb, passes laterally around the distal forearm to reach the anterolateral surface of the limb, and then continues proximally. It crosses the elbow, then passes up the arm into a triangular depression—the clavipectoral triangle (deltopectoral triangle)—between the pectoralis major muscle、deltoid muscle、and clavicle. In this depression, the vein passes into the axilla by penetrating deep fascia just inferior to the clavicle.

Basilic Vein

The basilic vein originates from the medial side of the dorsal venous network of the hand and passes proximally up the posteromedial surface of the forearm. It passes onto the anterior surface of the limb just inferior to the elbow and then continues proximally to penetrate deep fascia about midway up the arm.

Median Cubital Vein

At the elbow, the cephalic and basilic veins are connected by the median cubital vein, which crosses the roof of the cubital fossa.

臨床重點：淺層靜脈是臨床上抽取血液、建立靜脈通路及注射的首選位置。Cubital fossa 區域的 median cubital vein 特別常用，因其位置穩定且易於定位。

Shoulder（肩部）

The shoulder is the region of upper limb attachment to the trunk.

The bone framework of the shoulder consists of:

  • the clavicle and scapula, which form the pectoral girdle (shoulder girdle), and
  • the proximal end of the humerus.

The superficial muscles of the shoulder consist of the trapezius and deltoid muscles, which together form the smooth muscular contour over the lateral part of the shoulder. These muscles connect the scapula and clavicle to the trunk and to the arm, respectively.

Bones

Clavicle（鎖骨）

The clavicle is the only bony attachment between the trunk and the upper limb. It is palpable along its entire length and has a gentle S-shaped contour, with the forward-facing convex part medial and the forward-facing concave part lateral. The acromial (lateral) end of the clavicle is flat, whereas the sternal (medial) end is more robust and somewhat quadrangular in shape (Fig. 7.20).

The acromial end of the clavicle has a small oval facet on its surface for articulation with a similar facet on the medial surface of the acromion of the scapula.

The sternal end has a much larger facet for articulation mainly with the manubrium of the sternum, and to a lesser extent, with the first costal cartilage.

The inferior surface of the lateral third of the clavicle possesses a distinct tuberosity consisting of a tubercle (the conoid tubercle) and lateral roughening (the trapezoid line), for attachment of the important coracoclavicular ligament.

In addition, the surfaces and margins of the clavicle are roughened by the attachment of muscles that connect the clavicle to the thorax, neck, and upper limb. The superior surface is smoother than the inferior surface.

Scapula（肩胛骨）

The scapula is a large, flat triangular bone with:

  • three angles (lateral, superior, and inferior),
  • three borders (superior, lateral, and medial),
  • two surfaces (costal and posterior), and
  • three processes (acromion, spine, and coracoid process) (Fig. 7.21).

The lateral angle of the scapula is marked by a shallow, somewhat comma-shaped glenoid cavity, which articulates with the head of the humerus to form the glenohumeral joint (Fig. 7.21B,C).

A large triangular-shaped roughening (the infraglenoid tubercle) inferior to the glenoid cavity is the site of attachment for the long head of the triceps brachii muscle.

A less distinct supraglenoid tubercle is located superior to the glenoid cavity and is the site of attachment for the long head of the biceps brachii muscle.

A prominent spine subdivides the posterior surface of the scapula into a small, superior supraspinous fossa and a much larger, inferior infraspinous fossa (Fig. 7.21A).

The acromion, which is an anterolateral projection of the spine, arches over the glenohumeral joint and articulates, via a small oval facet on its distal end, with the clavicle.

The region between the lateral angle of the scapula and the attachment of the spine to the posterior surface of the scapula is the greater scapular notch (spinoglenoid notch).

Unlike the posterior surface, the costal surface of the scapula is unremarkable, being characterized by a shallow concave subscapular fossa over much of its extent (Fig. 7.21B). The costal surface and margins provide for muscle attachment, and the costal surface, together with its related muscle (subscapularis), moves freely over the underlying thoracic wall.

The lateral border of the scapula is strong and thick for muscle attachment, whereas the medial border and much of the superior border is thin and sharp.

The superior border is marked on its lateral end by:

  • the coracoid process, a hook-like structure that projects anterolaterally and is positioned directly inferior to the lateral part of the clavicle; and
  • the small but distinct suprascapular notch, which lies immediately medial to the root of the coracoid process.

The spine and acromion can be readily palpated on a patient, as can the tip of the coracoid process, the inferior angle, and much of the medial border of the scapula.

Proximal Humerus（肱骨近端）

The proximal end of the humerus consists of the head, the anatomical neck, the greater and lesser tubercles, the surgical neck, and the superior half of the shaft of the humerus (Fig. 7.22).

The head is half-spherical in shape and projects medially and somewhat superiorly to articulate with the much smaller glenoid cavity of the scapula.

The anatomical neck is very short and is formed by a narrow constriction immediately distal to the head. It lies between the head and the greater and lesser tubercles laterally, and between the head and the shaft more medially.

Greater and Lesser Tubercles（大小結節）

The greater and lesser tubercles are prominent landmarks on the proximal end of the humerus and serve as attachment sites for the four rotator cuff muscles of the glenohumeral joint.

The greater tubercle is lateral in position. Its superior surface and posterior surface are marked by three large smooth facets for muscle tendon attachments:

  • The superior facet is for attachment of the supraspinatus muscle.
  • The middle facet is for attachment of the infraspinatus.
  • The inferior facet is for attachment of the teres minor.

The lesser tubercle is anterior in position and its surface is marked by a large smooth impression for attachment of the subscapularis muscle.

A deep intertubercular sulcus (bicipital groove) separates the lesser and greater tubercles and continues inferiorly onto the proximal shaft of the humerus (Fig. 7.22). The tendon of the long head of the biceps brachii passes through this sulcus.

Roughenings on the lateral and medial lips and on the floor of the intertubercular sulcus mark sites for the attachment of the pectoralis major, teres major, and latissimus dorsi muscles, respectively.

The lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus is continuous inferiorly with a large V-shaped deltoid tuberosity on the lateral surface of the humerus midway along its length (Fig. 7.22), which is where the deltoid muscle inserts onto the humerus.

In approximately the same position, but on the medial surface of the bone, there is a thin vertical roughening for attachment of the coracobrachialis muscle.

Surgical Neck（外科頸）

One of the most important features of the proximal end of the humerus is the surgical neck (Fig. 7.22). This region is oriented in the horizontal plane between the expanded proximal part of the humerus (head, anatomical neck, and tubercles) and the narrower shaft. The axillary nerve and the posterior circumflex humeral artery, which pass into the deltoid region from the axilla, do so immediately posterior to the surgical neck. Because the surgical neck is weaker than more proximal regions of the bone, it is one of the sites where the humerus commonly fractures. The associated nerve (axillary) and artery (posterior circumflex humeral) can be damaged by fractures in this region.

臨床重點：Fracture of the proximal humerus（近端肱骨骨折）

It is extremely rare for fractures to occur across the anatomical neck of the humerus because the obliquity of such a fracture would have to traverse the thickest region of bone. Typically fractures occur around the surgical neck of the humerus. Although the axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery may be damaged with this type of fracture, this rarely happens. It is important that the axillary nerve is tested before relocation to be sure that the injury has not damaged the nerve and that the treatment itself does not cause a neurological deficit.

Joints

The three joints in the shoulder complex are the sternoclavicular、acromioclavicular、and glenohumeral joints.

The sternoclavicular joint and the acromioclavicular joint link the two bones of the pectoral girdle to each other and to the trunk. The combined movements at these two joints enable the scapula to be positioned over a wide range on the thoracic wall, substantially increasing “reach” by the upper limb.

The glenohumeral joint (shoulder joint) is the articulation between the humerus of the arm and the scapula.

Sternoclavicular Joint（胸鎖關節）

The sternoclavicular joint occurs between the proximal end of the clavicle and the clavicular notch of the manubrium of the sternum together with a small part of the first costal cartilage (Fig. 7.23). It is synovial and saddle shaped. The articular cavity is completely separated into two compartments by an articular disc. The sternoclavicular joint allows movement of the clavicle, predominantly in the anteroposterior and vertical planes, although some rotation also occurs.

The sternoclavicular joint is surrounded by a joint capsule and is reinforced by four ligaments:

  • The anterior and posterior sternoclavicular ligaments are anterior and posterior, respectively, to the joint.
  • An interclavicular ligament links the ends of the two clavicles to each other and to the superior surface of the manubrium of the sternum.
  • The costoclavicular ligament is positioned laterally to the joint and links the proximal end of the clavicle to the first rib and related costal cartilage.

Acromioclavicular Joint（肩鎖關節）

The acromioclavicular joint is a small synovial joint between an oval facet on the medial surface of the acromion and a similar facet on the acromial end of the clavicle (Fig. 7.24). It allows movement in the anteroposterior and vertical planes together with some axial rotation.

The acromioclavicular joint is surrounded by a joint capsule and is reinforced by:

  • a small acromioclavicular ligament superior to the joint and passing between adjacent regions of the clavicle and acromion, and
  • a much larger coracoclavicular ligament, which is not directly related to the joint, but is an important strong accessory ligament, providing much of the weight-bearing support for the upper limb on the clavicle and maintaining the position of the clavicle on the acromion—it spans the distance between the coracoid process of the scapula and the inferior surface of the acromial end of the clavicle and comprises an anterior trapezoid ligament (which attaches to the trapezoid line on the clavicle) and a posterior conoid ligament (which attaches to the related conoid tubercle).

Glenohumeral Joint（盂肱關節）

The glenohumeral joint is a synovial ball and socket articulation between the head of the humerus and the glenoid cavity of the scapula (Fig. 7.25). It is multiaxial with a wide range of movements provided at the cost of skeletal stability. Joint stability is provided, instead, by the rotator cuff muscles、the long head of the biceps brachii muscle、related bony processes, and extracapsular ligaments. Movements at the joint include flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, medial rotation, lateral rotation, and circumduction.

The articular surfaces of the glenohumeral joint are the large spherical head of the humerus and the small glenoid cavity of the scapula (Fig. 7.25). Each of the surfaces is covered by hyaline cartilage.

The glenoid cavity is deepened and expanded peripherally by a fibrocartilaginous collar (the glenoid labrum), which attaches to the margin of the fossa. Superiorly, this labrum is continuous with the tendon of the long head of the biceps brachii muscle, which attaches to the supraglenoid tubercle and passes through the articular cavity superior to the head of the humerus.

Synovial Membrane（滑膜）

The synovial membrane attaches to the margins of the articular surfaces and lines the fibrous membrane of the joint capsule (Fig. 7.26). The synovial membrane is loose inferiorly. This redundant region of synovial membrane and related fibrous membrane accommodates abduction of the arm.

The synovial membrane protrudes through apertures in the fibrous membrane to form bursae, which lie between the tendons of surrounding muscles and the fibrous membrane. The most consistent of these is the subtendinous bursa of the subscapularis, which lies between the subscapularis muscle and the fibrous membrane. The synovial membrane also folds around the tendon of the long head of the biceps brachii muscle in the joint and extends along the tendon as it passes into the intertubercular sulcus. All these synovial structures reduce friction between the tendons and adjacent joint capsule and bone.

In addition to bursae that communicate with the articular cavity through apertures in the fibrous membrane, other bursae are associated with the joint but are not connected to it. These occur:

  • between the acromion (or deltoid muscle) and supraspinatus muscle (or joint capsule) (the subacromial or subdeltoid bursa),
  • between the acromion and skin,
  • between the coracoid process and the joint capsule, and
  • in relationship to tendons of muscles around the joint (coracobrachialis, teres major, long head of triceps brachii, and latissimus dorsi muscles).
Fibrous Membrane（纖維膜）

The fibrous membrane of the joint capsule attaches to the margin of the glenoid cavity, outside the attachment of the glenoid labrum and the long head of the biceps brachii muscle, and to the anatomical neck of the humerus (Fig. 7.27).

On the humerus, the medial attachment occurs more inferiorly than the neck and extends onto the shaft. In this region, the fibrous membrane is also loose or folded in the anatomical position. This redundant area of the fibrous membrane accommodates abduction of the arm.

Openings in the fibrous membrane provide continuity of the articular cavity with bursae that occur between the joint capsule and surrounding muscles and around the tendon of the long head of the biceps brachii muscle in the intertubercular sulcus.

The fibrous membrane of the joint capsule is thickened:

  • anterosuperiorly in three locations to form superior, middle, and inferior glenohumeral ligaments, which pass from the superomedial margin of the glenoid cavity to the lesser tubercle and inferiorly related anatomical neck of the humerus (Fig. 7.27);
  • superiorly between the base of the coracoid process and the greater tubercle of the humerus (the coracohumeral ligament); and
  • between the greater and lesser tubercles of the humerus (transverse humeral ligament)—this holds the tendon of the long head of the biceps brachii muscle in the intertubercular sulcus (Fig. 7.27).
Joint Stability（關節穩定性）

Joint stability is provided by surrounding muscle tendons and a skeletal arch formed superiorly by the coracoid process and acromion and the coraco-acromial ligament (Fig. 7.28).

Tendons of the rotator cuff muscles (the supraspinatus、infraspinatus、teres minor、and subscapularis muscles) blend with the joint capsule and form a musculotendinous collar around the glenohumeral joint, effectively keeping the head of the humerus seated in the glenoid cavity.

臨床重點：The rotator cuff muscles are the primary stabilizers of the glenohumeral joint. Tears in these tendons—particularly the supraspinatus—are common causes of shoulder pain and dysfunction. The subacromial (subdeltoid) bursa is frequently involved in impingement syndromes, where inflammation of the bursa causes pain with arm elevation.

Upper Limb — Shoulder & Posterior Scapular Region

Glenohumeral Joint

The rotator cuff is a sleeve of muscle that surrounds the posterior, superior, and anterior aspects of the glenohumeral joint (Figs. 7.28 and 7.29). This cuff of muscles stabilizes and holds the head of the humerus in the glenoid cavity of the scapula without compromising the arm’s flexibility and range of motion. The tendon of the long head of the biceps brachii muscle passes superiorly through the joint and restricts upward movement of the humeral head on the glenoid cavity.

Infraspinatus

Vascular supply to the glenohumeral joint is predominantly through branches of the anterior and posterior circumflex humeral and suprascapular arteries.

The glenohumeral joint is innervated by branches from the posterior cord of the brachial plexus, and from the suprascapular, axillary, and lateral pectoral nerves.

臨床重點：Clavicle fractures are common due to the bone’s relative size and the forces transmitted from the upper limb to the trunk. The typical fracture site is the middle third of the clavicle. The medial and lateral thirds are rarely fractured.

臨床重點：Acromial end of the clavicle tends to dislocate at the acromioclavicular joint with trauma. A minor injury tears the fibrous joint capsule and ligaments of the acromioclavicular joint, resulting in acromioclavicular separation. More severe trauma disrupts the conoid and trapezoid ligaments of the coracoclavicular ligament, causing elevation and upward subluxation of the clavicle.

臨床重點：At the medial end of the clavicle, the typical injury is an anterior or posterior dislocation of the sternoclavicular joint. Importantly, a posterior dislocation of the clavicle may impinge on the great vessels in the root of the neck and compress or disrupt them.

Dislocations of the Glenohumeral Joint

The glenohumeral joint is extremely mobile, providing a wide range of movement at the expense of stability. The relatively small bony glenoid cavity, supplemented by the less robust fibrocartilaginous glenoid labrum and the ligamentous support, make it susceptible to dislocation.

臨床重點：Anterior dislocation (Fig. 7.32) occurs most frequently and is usually associated with an isolated traumatic incident (clinically, all anterior dislocations are anteroinferior). In some cases, the anteroinferior glenoid labrum is torn with or without a small bony fragment. Once the joint capsule and cartilage are disrupted, the joint is susceptible to further (recurrent) dislocations.

臨床重點：When an anteroinferior dislocation occurs, the axillary nerve may be injured by direct compression of the humeral head on the nerve inferiorly as it passes through the quadrangular space. Furthermore, the “lengthening” effect of the humerus may stretch the radial nerve, which is tightly bound within the radial groove, and produce a radial nerve paralysis.

臨床重點：Occasionally, an anteroinferior dislocation is associated with a fracture, which may require surgical reduction. Posterior dislocation is extremely rare; when seen, the clinician should focus on its cause, the most common being extremely vigorous muscle contractions associated with an epileptic seizure caused by electrocution.

Rotator Cuff Disorders

臨床重點：The two main disorders of the rotator cuff are impingement and tendinopathy. The muscle most commonly involved is supraspinatus as it passes beneath the acromion and the acromioclavicular ligament. This space, beneath which the supraspinatus tendon passes, is of fixed dimensions. Swelling of the supraspinatus muscle, excessive fluid within the subacromial/subdeltoid bursa, or subacromial bony spurs may produce significant impingement when the arm is abducted.

臨床重點：The blood supply to the supraspinatus tendon is relatively poor. Repeated trauma makes the tendon susceptible to degenerative change, which may result in calcium deposition, producing extreme pain.

臨床重點：When the supraspinatus tendon has undergone significant degenerative change, it is more susceptible to trauma, and partial- or full-thickness tears may develop (Fig. 7.33). These tears are most common in older patients and may result in considerable difficulty in carrying out normal activities of daily living such as combing hair. However, complete tears may be entirely asymptomatic.

Inflammation of the Subacromial (Subdeltoid) Bursa

臨床重點：Between the supraspinatus and deltoid muscles laterally and the acromion medially, there is a bursa referred to clinically as the subacromial or subdeltoid bursa. In patients who have injured the shoulder or who have supraspinatus tendinopathy, this bursa may become inflamed, making movements of the glenohumeral joint painful. These inflammatory changes may be treated by injection of a corticosteroid and local anesthetic agent.

Shoulder Muscles

The two most superficial muscles of the shoulder are the trapezius and deltoid muscles (Fig. 7.35 and Table 7.1). Together, they provide the characteristic contour of the shoulder:

  • The trapezius attaches the scapula and clavicle to the trunk.
  • The deltoid attaches the scapula and clavicle to the humerus.

Trapezius

The trapezius muscle has an extensive origin from the axial skeleton, which includes sites on the skull and the vertebrae, from CI to TXII (Fig. 7.36). From CI to CVII, the muscle attaches to the vertebrae through the ligamentum nuchae. The muscle inserts onto the skeletal framework of the shoulder along the inner margins of a continuous U-shaped line of attachment oriented in the horizontal plane, with the bottom of the U directed laterally. Together, the left and right trapezius muscles form a diamond or trapezoid shape, from which the name is derived.

The trapezius muscle is a powerful elevator of the shoulder and also rotates the scapula to extend the reach superiorly.

Innervation of the trapezius muscle is by the accessory nerve [XI] and the anterior rami of cervical nerves C3 and C4 (Fig. 7.36). These nerves pass vertically along the deep surface of the muscle. The accessory nerve can be evaluated by testing the function of the trapezius muscle. This is most easily done by asking patients to shrug their shoulders against resistance.

Deltoid

The deltoid muscle is large and triangular in shape, with its base attached to the scapula and clavicle and its apex attached to the humerus (Fig. 7.36). It originates along a continuous U-shaped line of attachment to the clavicle and the scapula, mirroring the adjacent insertion sites of the trapezius muscle. It inserts into the deltoid tuberosity on the lateral surface of the shaft of the humerus.

The major function of the deltoid muscle is abduction of the arm beyond the initial 15° accomplished by the supraspinatus muscle.

The deltoid muscle is innervated by the axillary nerve, which is a branch of the posterior cord of the brachial plexus. The axillary nerve and associated blood vessels (the posterior circumflex humeral artery and vein) enter the deltoid by passing posteriorly around the surgical neck of the humerus.

Levator Scapulae

The levator scapulae originates from the transverse processes of CI to CIV vertebrae (Fig. 7.36). It descends laterally to attach to the posterior surface of the medial border of the scapula from the superior angle to the smooth triangular area of bone at the root of the spine.

The levator scapulae muscle is innervated by the dorsal scapular nerve and directly from C3 and C4 spinal nerves. The levator scapulae elevates the scapula.

Rhomboid Minor and Major

The rhomboid minor and major muscles attach medially to the vertebral column and descend laterally to attach to the medial border of the scapula inferior to the levator scapulae muscle (Fig. 7.36).

  • The rhomboid minor originates from the lower end of the ligamentum nuchae and the spines of CVII and TI vertebrae. It inserts laterally into the smooth triangular area of bone at the root of the spine of the scapula on the posterior surface.
  • The rhomboid major originates from the spines of vertebrae TII to TV and from the intervening supraspinous ligaments. It descends laterally to insert along the posterior surface of the medial border of the scapula from the insertion of the rhomboid minor to the inferior angle.

The rhomboid muscles are innervated by the dorsal scapular nerve, which is a branch of the brachial plexus. The rhomboid minor and major retract and elevate the scapula.

Posterior Scapular Region

The posterior scapular region occupies the posterior aspect of the scapula and is located deep to the trapezius and deltoid muscles (Fig. 7.37 and Table 7.2). It contains four muscles, which pass between the scapula and proximal end of the humerus: the supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor, and teres major muscles.

The posterior scapular region also contains part of one additional muscle, the long head of the triceps brachii, which passes between the scapula and the proximal end of the forearm. This muscle, along with other muscles of the region and the humerus, participates in forming a number of spaces through which nerves and vessels enter and leave the region.

The supraspinatus, infraspinatus, and teres minor muscles are components of the rotator cuff, which stabilizes the glenohumeral joint.

Muscles of the Posterior Scapular Region

Supraspinatus and Infraspinatus

The supraspinatus and infraspinatus muscles originate from two large fossae, one above and one below the spine, on the posterior surface of the scapula (Fig. 7.37). They form tendons that insert on the greater tubercle of the humerus.

  • The tendon of the supraspinatus passes under the acromion, where it is separated from the bone by a subacromial bursa, passes over the glenohumeral joint, and inserts on the superior facet of the greater tubercle.
  • The tendon of the infraspinatus passes posteriorly to the glenohumeral joint and inserts on the middle facet of the greater tubercle.

The supraspinatus initiates abduction of the arm. The infraspinatus laterally rotates the humerus.

Teres Minor and Teres Major

The teres minor muscle is a cord-like muscle that originates from a flattened area of the scapula immediately adjacent to its lateral border below the infraglenoid tubercle (Fig. 7.37). Its tendon inserts on the inferior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus. The teres minor laterally rotates the humerus and is a component of the rotator cuff.

The teres major muscle originates from a large oval region on the posterior surface of the inferior angle of the scapula (Fig. 7.37). This broad cord-like muscle passes superiorly and laterally and ends as a flat tendon that attaches to the medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus on the anterior surface of the humerus. The teres major medially rotates and extends the humerus.

Long Head of Triceps Brachii

The long head of the triceps brachii muscle originates from the infraglenoid tubercle and passes somewhat vertically down the arm to insert, with the medial and lateral heads of this muscle, on the olecranon of the ulna (Fig. 7.37).

The triceps brachii is the primary extensor of the forearm at the elbow joint. Because the long head crosses the glenohumeral joint, it can also extend and adduct the humerus.

The importance of the triceps brachii in the posterior scapular region is that its vertical course between the teres minor and teres major, together with these muscles and the humerus, forms spaces through which nerves and vessels pass between regions.

Gateways to the Posterior Scapular Region

Suprascapular Foramen

The suprascapular foramen is the route through which structures pass between the base of the neck and the posterior scapular region (Fig. 7.37). It is formed by the suprascapular notch of the scapula and the superior transverse scapular (suprascapular) ligament, which converts the notch into a foramen.

The suprascapular nerve passes through the suprascapular foramen; the suprascapular artery and the suprascapular vein follow the same course as the nerve, but normally pass immediately superior to the superior transverse scapular ligament and not through the foramen (Fig. 7.38).

Quadrangular Space

The quadrangular space provides a passageway for nerves and vessels passing between more anterior regions (the axilla) and the posterior scapular region (Fig. 7.37). In the posterior scapular region, its boundaries are formed by:

  • The inferior margin of the teres minor
  • The surgical neck of the humerus
  • The superior margin of the teres major
  • The lateral margin of the long head of the triceps brachii

The axillary nerve and the posterior circumflex humeral artery and vein pass through this space (Fig. 7.38).

Teres minor Upper two-thirds of a flattened strip of bone on the posterior surface of the scapula immediately adjacent to the lateral border of the scapula Inferior facet on the posterior surface of the greater tubercle of the humerus Axillary nerve (C5, C6) Rotator cuff muscle; lateral rotation of arm at glenohumeral joint
Teres major Elongate oval area on the posterior surface of the inferior angle of the scapula Medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus on the anterior surface of the humerus Inferior subscapular nerve (C5, C6, C7) Medial rotation and extension of the arm at the glenohumeral joint
Long head of triceps brachii Infraglenoid tubercle on scapula Common tendon of insertion with medial and lateral heads on the olecranon process of ulna Radial nerve (C6, C7, C8) Extension of the forearm at the elbow joint; accessory adductor and extensor of the arm at the glenohumeral joint

Upper Limb — Posterior Scapular Region & Axilla

Triangular Space（三角間隙）

The triangular space 是肩胛後區與腋窩之間的 comunication area（圖 7.37）。

從肩胛後區觀察，triangular space 的邊界為：

  • long head of triceps brachii（肱三頭肌長頭）的內側緣
  • teres major（大圓肌）的上緣
  • teres minor（小圓肌）的下緣

Circumflex scapular artery 與靜脈通過此間隙（圖 7.38）。

Triangular Interval（三角窗）

Triangular interval 的邊界為：

  • long head of triceps brachii（肱三頭肌長頭）的外側緣
  • humerus（肱骨）的骨幹
  • teres major（大圓肌）的下緣（圖 7.37）

由於此空間低於界定腋窩下界的 teres major 下緣，因此 triangular interval 作為：

  • 上臂前、後筋膜室之間的通道
  • 上臂後筋膜室與腋窩之間的通道

Radial nerve、profunda brachii artery（上臂深动脉）及相關靜脈通過此處（圖 7.38）。

Nerves（神經）

Posterior Scapular Region 的兩條主要神經為 suprascapular nerve 與 axillary nerve，兩者皆起源於腋窩中的 brachial plexus（臂神經叢）（圖 7.38）。

Suprascapular Nerve

Suprascapular nerve 起源於頸根（base of neck），由 brachial plexus 的上幹發出。從起始處向後外側走行，穿過 suprascapular foramen 到達肩胛後區，介於骨與肌肉之間（圖 7.38）。

  • 支配 supraspinatus muscle（岡上肌）
  • 隨後穿過 greater scapular (spinoglenoid) notch（肩胛大切跡），位於肩胛棘根部與關節盂之間，終止並支配 infraspinatus muscle（岡下肌）

通常 suprascapular nerve 無皮枝。

Axillary Nerve

Axillary nerve 起源於 brachial plexus 的後束。經由腋窩後壁的 quadrangular space 離開腋窩，進入肩胛後區（圖 7.38）。

  • 與 posterior circumflex humeral artery 與靜脈伴行
  • 與 humerus surgical neck（肱骨外科頸）的後表面直接相鄰

Axillary nerve 支配 deltoid（三角肌）與 teres minor（小圓肌）。此外，有一皮枝——superior lateral cutaneous nerve of the arm，支配三角肌下部表面的皮膚感覺。

Arteries and Veins（動脈與靜脈）

Posterior Scapular Region 有三條主要 arteries：

  • Suprascapular artery
  • Posterior circumflex humeral artery
  • Circumflex scapular artery

這些 arteries 在肩胛周圍形成互聯的血管網絡（圖 7.39）。

Suprascapular Artery

Suprascapular artery 起源於頸根，為 thyrocervical trunk（甲狀頸幹）的分支——而 thyrocervical trunk 是 subclavian artery（鎖骨下動脈）的主要分支（圖 7.38、7.39）。此血管也可能直接起源於 subclavian artery 的第三段。

正常情況下，suprascapular artery 在 suprascapular foramen 上方進入肩胛後區，而神經則穿過此 foramen。在肩胛後區，血管與 suprascapular nerve 伴行。

除供應 supraspinatus 與 infraspinatus muscles 外，suprascapular artery 沿途還分出 branches 至多個結構。

Posterior Circumflex Humeral Artery

Posterior circumflex humeral artery 起源於腋窩中 axillary artery 的第三段（圖 7.39）。

此 artery 與 axillary nerve 經由腋窩後壁的 quadrangular space 離開腋窩，進入肩胛後區。供應相關肌肉及 glenohumeral joint（盂肱關節）。

Circumflex Scapular Artery

Circumflex scapular artery 為 subscapular artery 的分支，亦起源於腋窩中 axillary artery 的第三段（圖 7.39）。此 artery 經由 triangular space 離開腋窩，進入肩胛後區，穿過 teres minor muscle 的起始部，與區域內其他 arteries 形成吻合連接。

Veins（靜脈）

Posterior scapular region 的靜脈大致伴行 arteries，並與頸部、背部、上臂及腋窩的血管相連。

臨床重點：Quadrangular Space Syndrome（四邊隙症候群）

Quadrangular space（四邊隙）肌肉肥大或肌肉邊緣纖維化可能壓迫 axillary nerve。少見情況下導致 deltoid muscle 無力。通常引起 teres minor muscle 萎縮，進而影響旋轉袖肌群對肩關節運動的控制。

AXILLA（腋窩）

Axilla 是上肢的門戶，提供頸部與上臂之間的過渡區域（圖 7.40A）。由 clavicle（鎖骨）、scapula（肩胛骨）、上胸壁、humerus 及相關肌肉所形成的 irregilarly shaped pyramidal space（四邊不規則的錐體空間），具有：

  • 四面牆（walls）
  • 一個入口（inlet）
  • 一個底部（floor/base）（圖 7.40A、B）

腋窩入口上方與頸部相續，底部外側向上臂開放。所有進出上肢的主要結構皆通過腋窩（圖 7.40C）。前、後壁肌肉之間形成的 apertures 使結構得以在腋窩與相鄰區域（肩胛後區、胸肌區、三角肌區）之間通行。

Axillary Inlet（腋窩入口）

Axillary inlet 位於水平面，大致呈三角形，頂尖指向外側（圖 7.40A、B）。入口邊緣完全由骨頭構成：

  • 內側緣：第一肋骨（rib I）的外側界
  • 前緣：clavicle 的後表面
  • 後緣：肩胛上緣至喙突（coracoid process）

三角形腋窩入口的頂尖位於外側，由 coracoid process 的內側面構成。

主要血管與神經在頸部與腋窩之間通行時，需跨越 rib I 的外側緣並穿過腋窩入口（圖 7.40A）。

  • Subclavian artery（鎖骨下動脈）在跨越 rib I 外側緣並進入腋窩後，延續為 axillary artery（腋窩動脈）
  • Axillary vein（腋窩靜脈）在跨越 rib I 並離開腋窩進入頸部後，延續為 subclavian vein（鎖骨下靜脈）

在腋窩入口處，axillary vein 位於 axillary artery 的前方，而 artery 位於 brachial plexus 神經幹的前方。

Brachial plexus 的下幹（inferior trunk）位於頸部 rib I 的正上方，subclavian artery 與靜脈亦然。當它們跨越 rib I 時，靜脈與 artery 被 anterior scalene muscle（前斜角肌）的插入點分開（圖 7.40A）。

Anterior Wall（前壁）

腋窩前壁由以下結構組成（表 7.3）：

  • Pectoralis major muscle（胸大肌）
  • Pectoralis minor muscle（胸小肌）
  • Subclavius muscle（鎖骨下肌）
  • Clavipectoral fascia（鎖胸筋膜）

Muscles of the Anterior Wall（前壁肌肉）

Muscle Origin Insertion Innervation Function
Pectoralis major Clavicular head：鎖骨內側半的前表面；Sternocostal head：胸骨前表面、第一至第七肋軟骨、第六肋骨的胸骨端、外斜肌的腱膜 肱骨 intertubercular sulcus 的外側唇 Medial 與 Lateral pectoral nerves；Clavicular head（C5, C6）；Sternocostal head（C6, C7, C8, T1） 在 glenohumeral joint 屈曲、內收、內旋上臂；Clavicular head：使伸直的上臂屈曲；Sternocostal head：使屈曲的上臂伸直
Subclavius 第一肋骨，位於肋骨與肋軟骨交界處 鎖骨中三分之一下表面的淺溝 Nerve to subclavius（C5, C6） 向下拉肩部尖端（壓低鎖骨）；向內拉鎖骨以穩定胸鎖關節
Pectoralis minor 第三至第五肋骨前表面及上緣；覆蓋相鄰肋間隙的深筋膜 肩胛骨 coracoid process（內側緣及上表面） Medial pectoral nerve（C5, C6, C7, C8, T1） 向下拉肩部尖端；向前拉肩胛骨
Pectoralis Major

Pectoralis major 是前壁最大、最淺層的肌肉（圖 7.41）。其下緣構成 anterior axillary fold（前腋皺襞），是腋窩的前下界。此肌肉有兩個頭：

  • Clavicular head：起源於 clavicle 的內側半
  • Sternocostal head：起源於胸廓前壁的內側部——通常此頭的纖維繼續向下、向內延伸，附著於腹壁，形成肌肉的腹部部分

肌肉插入肱骨 intertubercular sulcus 的外側唇。起源於軀幹上方的部分，插入位置較低且較前方；起源於下方的部分，插入位置較高。

兩頭共同作用時，pectralis major 在 glenohumeral joint 使上臂屈曲、內收、內旋。Clavicular head 使上臂從伸直位置屈曲；Sternocostal head 使上臂從屈曲位置伸直（尤其在抗阻力時）。

由起源於腋窩內 brachial plexus 的 lateral 與 medial pectoral nerves 支配。

Subclavius

Subclavius 是一塊位於 pectoralis major 深層的小肌肉，介於 clavicle 與第一肋骨之間（圖 7.42）。以肌腱形式從第一肋骨與肋軟骨交界處起始，向外側並向上走行，以肌性附著插入鎖骨中三分之一下表面的狹淺溝內。

功能尚不完全清楚，可能作用為：

  • 通過壓低鎖骨向下拉肩部
  • 通過向內拉鎖骨穩定胸鎖關節

由起源於 brachial plexus 上幹的小分支支配。

Pectoralis Minor

Pectoralis minor 是一塊位於 pectoralis major 深層的三角形肌肉，從胸壁延伸至肩胛骨的 coracoid process（圖 7.42）。以三個肌腹形式起源於第三至第五肋骨的前表面及上緣，以及覆蓋相鄰肋間隙的深筋膜。肌纖維向上、外側走行，插入 coracoid process 的內側及上部。

此肌肉向前拉肩胛骨（使肩胛骨在胸壁上向前滑動），並壓低肩胛骨的外側角。

由起源於腋窩內 brachial plexus 的 medial pectoral nerve 支配。

Clavipectoral Fascia（鎖胸筋膜）

Clavipectoral fascia 是一片厚的結締組織膜，連接 clavicle 與腋窩底部（圖 7.42）。包繞 subclavius 與 pectoralis minor muscles，並跨越兩者之間的間隙。

結構在腋窩與前壁之間通行時，需穿過 clavipectoral fascia，方式為：

  • 在 subclavius 與 pectoralis minor muscles 之間，或
  • 在 pectoralis minor muscle 下方

穿過 subclavius 與 pectoralis minor 之間的重要結構包括：cephalic vein（頭靜脈）、thoraco-acromial artery（胸肩峰動脈）、lateral pectoral nerve。

Lateral thoracic artery 通過 pectoralis minor 下方穿過筋膜離開腋窩。

Medial pectoral nerve 穿過 pectoralis minor 直接進入該肌肉以支配之，並到達 pectoralis major。偶爾，medial pectoral nerve 的分支繞過 pectoralis minor 的下緣到達並支配覆蓋其上的 pectoralis major。

Medial Wall（內側壁）

腋窩內側壁由上胸壁（肋骨及相關肋間組織）與 serratus anterior muscle（前鋸肌）組成（圖 7.43、表 7.4）。

Serratus Anterior

Serratus anterior 以多個肌腹形式起源於第一至第九肋骨的外側面及覆蓋相鄰肋間隙的深筋膜（圖 7.43）。肌肉形成扁平 sheet，繞過胸壁向後延伸，主要附著於肩胛骨內側緣的肋面。

Serratus anterior 向前拉肩胛骨，使其在胸壁上滑動，並促進肩胛骨的旋轉。它亦使肩胛骨的肋面與胸壁緊密相貼。

由 long thoracic nerve（胸長神經）支配——此神經源自 brachial plexus 的根部，沿內側壁通過腋窩，沿 serratus anterior 的外表面垂直下行，位於皮膚與淺筋膜的深層。

Intercostobrachial Nerve

穿過內側壁直接進入腋窩的唯一主要結構是 intercostobrachial nerve（圖 7.43）。此神經是第二肋間神經的外側皮支（T2 的前支）。在腋窩內與 brachial plexus 的分支（medial cutaneous nerve of the arm）交通，供應上臂後內側的皮膚，屬於 T2 皮節。

臨床重點：Scapular “Winging”（肩胛翼狀變形）

由於 long thoracic nerve 沿胸壁外側面下行於 serratus anterior 的外表面，位於皮膚與皮下筋膜的深層，因此容易受損。此肌肉功能喪失導致肩胛骨內側緣（尤其是下角）抬起離開胸壁，在上臂向前推時產生典型的肩胛骨「翼狀」外觀。此外，正常的上臂抬高動作也無法完成。

Muscles of the Medial Wall（內側壁肌肉）

Muscle Origin Insertion Innervation Function
Serratus anterior 上 8-9 肋骨的外側面及覆蓋相鄰肋間隙的深筋膜 肩胛骨內側緣的肋面 Long thoracic nerve（C5, C6, C7） 拉肩胛骨向前並旋轉；使肩胛骨內側緣及下角與胸壁相貼

Lateral Wall（外側壁）

腋窩外側壁狹窄，完全由 humerus 的 intertubercular sulcus（結節間溝）構成（圖 7.44）。

  • 前壁的 pectoralis major 附著於 intertubercular sulcus 的外側唇
  • 後壁的 latissimus dorsi 與 teres major 分別附著於 sulcus 的底部與內側唇（表 7.5）

Posterior Wall（後壁）

腋窩後壁結構複雜（圖 7.45，另見圖 7.50）。其骨框架由肩胛骨的肋面構成。後壁的肌肉包括：

  • Subscapularis muscle（肩胛下肌）：附著於肩胛骨的肋面
  • Latissimus dorsi 與 teres major 的遠端部分：從背部及肩胛後區進入後壁
  • Long head of triceps brachii 的近端部分：垂直下行穿過後壁進入上臂

後壁肌肉之間的間隙形成 apertures，結構得以在腋窩、肩胛後區與上臂後筋膜室之間通行。

Muscles of the Lateral and Posterior Walls（外側壁與後壁肌肉）

Muscle Origin Insertion Innervation Function
Subscapularis Subscapular fossa 的內側三分之二 肱骨小結節 Upper 與 Lower subscapular nerves（C5, C6, (C7)） 旋轉袖肌；在 glenohumeral joint 使上臂內旋
Teres major 肩胛骨下角後表面的狹長橢圓形區域 肱骨前表面 intertubercular sulcus 的內側唇 Lower subscapular nerve（C5, C6, C7） 在 glenohumeral joint 使上臂內旋、伸直、內收
Latissimus dorsi 下六個胸椎的棘突及相關棘間韌帶；經胸腰筋膜至腰椎棘突、相關棘間韌帶及髂嵴；下 3-4 肋骨 Intertubercular sulcus 的底部 Thoracodorsal nerve（C6, C7, C8） 在 glenohumeral joint 使上臂內收、內旋、伸直
Long head of triceps brachii 肩胛骨的 infraglenoid tubercule 與內側頭、外側頭共同腱性附著於尺骨鷹嘴突 Radial nerve（C6, C7, C8） 在肘關節伸直前臂；在 glenohumeral joint 輔助內收、伸直上臂

Arterial Anastomoses Around the Shoulder（肩關節周圍的动脉吻合）

肩關節周圍的arterial anastomoses（动脉吻合）如圖 7.39 所示。

主要吻合 arterials 包括：

  • Suprascapular artery
  • Subscapular artery
  • Anterior circumflex humeral artery
  • Posterior circumflex humeral artery
  • Circumflex scapular artery

這些 arteries 在肩胛骨周圍形成一個互聯的血管網絡，確保上肢的側支循環。

Gray’s Anatomy — Head & Neck

Regional Anatomy — Axilla（腋窩）

後壁（Posterior Wall）

Subscapularis Muscle（肩胛下肌）

Subscapularis 構成腋窩後壁的最大部分，起源於 subscapular fossa（肩胛下窩），附著於 humerus（肱骨） 的 lesser tubercle（小結節）（圖 7.45 與 7.46）。肌腱於 glenohumeral joint（盂肱關節） 關節囊前方通過。

肩胛下肌與後肩胛區的三塊肌肉（supraspinatus（棘上肌）、infraspinatus（棘下肌）、teres minor（小圓肌））同屬於 rotator cuff（旋轉袖） 肌群，穩定 glenohumeral joint。

肩胛下肌由臂神經叢分支（superior subscapular nerve 與 inferior subscapular nerve）支配，這些神經起源於腋窩。

Teres Major（大圓肌）與 Latissimus Dorsi（背闊肌）

腋窩後壁的外下側由 teres major muscle 的終末部分與 latissimus dorsi muscle 的扁平腱膜構成（圖 7.45）。這兩個結構位於 posterior axillary fold（後腋皺襞） 下方，標誌著腋窩的後下界。

Latissimus dorsi 的扁平腱膜繞過 teres major 的下緣，於後壁向前附著於 humerus 的 intertubercular sulcus（結節間溝） 底部，位置略上方高於 teres major 附著於結節間溝內側唇的最遠端附著點。因此，teres major 的下緣定義了腋窩外側的下界。

Axillary artery（腋動脈） 在越過 teres major 下緣後延續為 brachial artery（臂動脈）。

Long Head of Triceps Brachii（肱三頭肌長頭）

Triceps brachii 的長頭垂直穿過腋窩後壁，與周圍肌肉及相鄰骨頭共同形成三個孔隙，為主要結構通過後壁提供通道：

  • Quadrangular space（四邊形空間）
  • Triangular space（三角形空間）
  • Triangular interval（三角形間隙）（圖 7.45）

後壁的通道（Gateways in the Posterior Wall）

另見「後肩胛區的通道」，第 717–721 頁，及圖 7.37 與 7.38。

Quadrangular Space（四邊形空間）

四邊形空間為神經與血管在腋窩與更後方的肩胛區及三角肌區之間提供通道（圖 7.45）。從前方觀察，其邊界由以下結構形成：

  • Subscapularis muscle 的下緣
  • Humerus 的 surgical neck（外科頸）
  • Teres major muscle 的上緣
  • Triceps brachii 長頭的外側緣

通過四邊形空間的結構：Axillary nerve（腋神經） 與 posterior circumflex humeral artery（旋肱後動脈） 和靜脈。

Triangular Space（三角形空間）

三角形空間是腋窩與後肩胛區之間的交通區域（圖 7.45）。從前方觀察，由以下結構形成：

  • Triceps brachii 長頭的內側緣
  • Teres major muscle 的上緣
  • Subscapularis muscle 的下緣

Circumflex scapular artery（旋肩胛動脈） 與靜脈通過此空間。

Triangular Interval（三角形間隙）

此三角形間隙由以下結構形成：

  • Triceps brachii 長頭的外側緣
  • Humerus 的骨幹（shaft）
  • Teres major muscle 的下緣（圖 7.45）

Radial nerve（橈神經） 離開腋窩，經由此間隙進入臂的後間隔。

底（Floor）

腋窩的底由筋膜與一片拱形的皮膚構成，跨越各壁的下緣之間的距離（圖 7.47 並見圖 7.40B）。底由 clavipectoral fascia（鎖胸筋膜） 支撐。在患者身上，anterior axillary fold（前腋皺襞） 的位置比 posterior axillary fold（後腋皺襞） 更高。

下方，結構在底的外側進入和離開腋窩，此處前壁與後壁會合，腋窩與臂的前間隔相延續。

腋窩的內容物（Contents of the Axilla）

通過腋窩的是上肢的主要血管、神經與淋巴管。此空間也容納臂的兩塊肌肉的近端部分、乳腺的腋尾部及淋巴結群，引流上肢、胸壁與乳腺。

Biceps brachii（肱二頭肌） 與 Coracobrachialis（喙肱肌） 的近端部分通過腋窩（表 7.6）。

臨床重點：腋窩淋巴結引流上肢、胸壁與乳腺的淋巴。乳腺癌時，腋窩淋巴結清除術是重要的分期與治療步驟。

表 7.6 通過腋窩的肌肉

肌肉 起源 附著 支配 功能
Biceps brachii 長頭：scapula 的 supraglenoid tubercle；短頭：coracoid process 的 apex Radius 的 radial tuberosity Musculocutaneous nerve（C5, C6） 前臂於肘關節的強大屈肌與旋後肌；於 glenohumeral joint 的輔助屈臂肌
Coracobrachialis Coracoid process 的 apex Humerus 中段的線性粗糙區 Musculocutaneous nerve（C5, C6, C7） 於 glenohumeral joint 的屈臂肌；於內側收臂

腋窩內容物：肌肉（Contents of the Axilla: Muscles）

Biceps Brachii（肱二頭肌）

Biceps brachii 以兩個頭起源（圖 7.48）：

  • 短頭 起源於 scapula 的 coracoid process（喙突） apex，垂直通過腋窩進入臂部，與長頭會合。
  • 長頭 以肌腱起源於 scapula 的 supraglenoid tubercle（盂上結節），於 humerus 頭部深方通過 glenohumeral joint 關節囊，進入 intertubercular sulcus，由 transverse humeral ligament（橫肱韌帶） 固定於大結節與小結節之間；肌腱通過腋窩的結節間溝，於臂近端形成肌腹。

肌肉的長頭與短頭於臂遠端會合，主要以單一肌腱附著於前臂的 radial tuberosity（橈骨粗隆）。

Biceps brachii 主要為前臂於肘關節的強大屈肌與前臂的強大旋後肌。因為兩個頭都起源於 scapula，該肌肉也是臂於 glenohumeral joint 的輔助屈肌。此外，長頭防止 humerus 於 glenoid cavity 向上移動。

Biceps brachii 由 musculocutaneous nerve（肌皮神經） 支配。

Coracobrachialis（喙肱肌）

Coracobrachialis 與 biceps brachii 的短頭共同起源於 coracoid process 的 apex（圖 7.48）。它垂直通過腋窩，附著於 humerus 內側面大約中段的線性粗糙區。

Coracobrachialis 於 glenohumeral joint 屈臂。

在腋窩中，coracobrachialis 的內側面被 musculocutaneous nerve 穿過，該神經支配後通過肌肉進入臂部。

腋窩內容物：Axillary Artery（腋動脈）

Axillary artery 供應腋窩壁及相關區域，並作為上肢更遠端部分的主要血液供應（圖 7.49）。

頸部的 subclavian artery（鎖骨下動脈） 在 rib I（第一肋） 的外側緣變為 axillary artery，穿過腋窩，在 teres major muscle 的下緣延續為 brachial artery。

Axillary artery 被越過其前方的 pectoralis minor muscle（胸小肌） 分為三部分（圖 7.49）：

  • 第一部分：在 pectoralis minor 的近端
  • 第二部分：在 pectoralis minor 的後方
  • 第三部分：在 pectoralis minor 的遠端

一般而言，腋動脈有六條分支：

  • 第一部分：Superior thoracic artery（胸上動脈）
  • 第二部分：Thoraco-acromial artery（胸肩峰動脈） 與 lateral thoracic artery（胸外側動脈）
  • 第三部分：Subscapular artery（肩胛下動脈）、anterior circumflex humeral artery（旋肱前動脈） 與 posterior circumflex humeral artery（旋肱後動脈）（圖 7.50）

Superior Thoracic Artery（胸上動脈）

Superior thoracic artery 較細，起源於 axillary artery 第一部分的前表面（圖 7.50）。供應內側與前腋窩壁上區域。

Thoraco-Acromial Artery（胸肩峰動脈）

Thoraco-acromial artery 較短，起源於 axillary artery 第二部分的前表面，正好在 pectoralis minor 的內側（上方）緣後方（圖 7.50）。它繞過肌肉的上緣，穿過 clavipectoral fascia（鎖胸筋膜），立即分為四個分支——pectoral branch（胸肌支）、deltoid branch（三角肌支）、clavicular branch（鎖骨支） 與 acromial branch（肩峰支），供應前腋窩壁及相關區域。

此外，pectoral branch 為乳腺提供血液供應，deltoid branch 進入 clavipectoral triangle（鎖胸三角），與 cephalic vein（頭靜脈） 伴行並供應相鄰結構（見圖 7.41）。

Lateral Thoracic Artery（胸外側動脈）

Lateral thoracic artery 起源於 axillary artery 第二部分的前表面，在 pectoralis minor 的外側（下方）緣後方（圖 7.50）。它沿肌肉邊緣走向胸壁，供應腋窩的內側壁與前壁。在女性，分支從 pectoralis major（胸大肌） 下緣周圍走出，為乳腺的血液供應做出貢獻。

Subscapular Artery（肩胛下動脈）

Subscapular artery 是 axillary artery 最大的分支，是腋窩後壁的主要血液供應（圖 7.50）。它也為後肩胛區的血液供應做出貢獻。

Subscapular artery 起源於 axillary artery 第三部分的後表面，沿 subscapularis muscle 的下緣短距離行走，然後分為兩個終支：circumflex scapular artery 與 thoracodorsal artery（胸背動脈）。

  • Circumflex scapular artery 通過 subscapularis、teres major 與 triceps 長頭之間的三角形空間。後方，它從 teres minor 起源的下方穿過或穿過它進入 infraspinous fossa（岡下窩）。它與 suprascapular artery（棘上動脈） 及 transverse cervical artery（頸橫動脈） 的深支（dorsal scapular artery）吻合，為肩胛骨周圍的血管吻合網絡做出貢獻。
  • Thoracodorsal artery 大致沿肩胛骨外側緣走向下角。它為腋窩後壁與內側壁的血液供應做出貢獻。

Anterior Circumflex Humeral Artery（旋肱前動脈）

Anterior circumflex humeral artery 比 posterior circumflex humeral artery 細，起源於 axillary artery 第三部分的外側（圖 7.50）。它於 humerus 的 surgical neck 前方通過，與 posterior circumflex humeral artery 吻合。

此动脉為周圍組織（包括 glenohumeral joint 與 humerus 頭）供應分支。

Posterior Circumflex Humeral Artery（旋肱後動脈）

Posterior circumflex humeral artery 起源於 axillary artery 第三部分的外側表面，正好在 anterior circumflex humeral artery 起點的後方（圖 7.50）。它與 axillary nerve 一起，通過 teres major、teres minor、triceps brachii 長頭與 humerus 的 surgical neck 之間的四邊形空間離開腋窩。

Posterior circumflex humeral artery 繞過 humerus 的 surgical neck，為周圍肌肉與 glenohumeral joint 供應。它與 anterior circumflex humeral artery 以及來自 profunda brachii、suprascapular 與 thoraco-acromial arteries 的分支吻合。

Axillary Vein（腋靜脈）

Axillary vein 起於 teres major muscle 的下緣，是 basilic vein（貴要靜脈） 的延續（圖 7.51），貴要靜脈是引流手與前臂後內側面的淺靜脈，在臂中段穿透深筋膜。

Axillary vein 在腋窩中於 axillary artery 的內側與前方通過，在血管越過 rib I 外側緣的腋窩入口處延續為 subclavian vein（鎖骨下靜脈）。腋靜脈的屬支通常跟隨 axillary artery 的分支。其他屬支包括跟隨 brachial artery 的 brachial veins 與 cephalic vein（頭靜脈）。

Cephalic vein 是引流手部後外側與後部、前臂與臂部的淺靜脈。在肩部區域，它進入 deltoid muscle、pectoralis major 與 clavicle 之間的倒三角形裂隙（clavipectoral triangle）。在 clavipectoral triangle 的上部，cephalic vein 穿過 pectoralis major 的鎖骨頭深方，穿透 clavipectoral fascia 加入 axillary vein。

臨床重點：許多病情危重的患者失血或失液，需要補充。靜脈通路是補充液體的必要手段。典型的靜脈通路部位是手部的 cephalic vein 或肘窩（cubital fossa）淺層組織中的靜脈。

臨床重點：上肢血液供應的影像學檢查

臨床重點：當有臨床上血管受損的證據，或需要建立動靜脈瘻管（血液透析所需）時，需要影像學檢查來評估血管。

超聲波 是對上肢血管進行非侵入性評估的有用工具，可評估從 subclavian artery 第三部分到深部與淺部掌弓的血管。可以量化血流並記錄解剖變異。

血管造影 在某些情況下進行。於腹股溝韌帶下方穿刺股總動脈，將長導管經髂动脉繞過主動脈弓進入左鎖骨下动脉或頭臂幹再到右鎖骨下动脉。將不透射線的對比劑注入血管，在對比劑首先通過动脉、毛細血管最後到達靜脈時拍攝X光片。

臨床重點：上肢动脉外傷

臨床重點：上肢的动脉供應在相對固定或皮下位置特別容易受到外傷。

第一肋骨骨折

當 subclavian artery 從頸部穿出進入腋窩時，被周圍肌肉固定於 rib I 的上表面。上胸部創傷導致的快速減速損傷可能造成第一肋骨骨折，可能嚴重影響 subclavian artery 的遠端部分或 axillary artery 的第一部分。幸運的是，subclavian artery 與 axillary artery 分支之間存在吻合連接，在肩胛骨與肱骨近端周圍形成血管網絡；因此，即使完全血管切斷，臂也很少完全缺血（缺血是指器官或肢體的血液供應不良）。

肱骨頭前脫位

肱骨頭前脫位 可能壓迫 axillary artery，導致血管閉塞。這不太可能使上肢完全缺血，但可能需要手術重建 axillary artery 以獲得無痛功能。重要的是，axillary artery 與 brachial plexus（臂神經叢） 密切相關，在前脫位時可能受損。

臨床重點：Subclavian/Axillary 靜脈通路

臨床重點：有多种途径可以获得中心静脉通路。「锁骨下途径」和颈静脉途径是临床常用的方法。锁骨下途径这个名称虽然不够准确，但在临床实践中仍然是首选术语。事实上，大多数临床医生进入的是腋静脉的第一部分。

需要进行 subclavian vein/axillary vein 導管置入的患者有許多例。

進入 subclavian vein/axillary vein 是相對簡單的技術。識別鎖骨，在鎖骨下區放置銳利針頭，指向內上。當抽吸到靜脈血時，即獲得通路。此途徑常用於長期靜脈通路（如 Hickman 管）和短期通路（多種腔導管插入，如重症監護室）。

Subclavian vein/axillary vein 也是起搏器導線植入的首選部位。然而，有一個首選的進入點以防止併發症。應在鎖骨中線或此線的外側穿刺靜脈。這樣做的原因是靜脈的路徑及其與其他結構的關係。靜脈在走向胸廓入口時，位於动脉前方、第一肋上方、鎖骨下方。鎖骨下方有 subclavius muscle（鎖骨下肌）。如果穿刺部位正好在 subclavius muscle 與 axillary vein 相關之處，導管或導線可能在此處打折。而且，這塊肌肉持續的收縮與放鬆會導致管線疲勞，最終可能導致斷裂。斷裂的起搏器導線或化療導管破裂可能對患者造成嚴重後果。

Brachial Plexus（臂神經叢）

Brachial plexus 是由 C5 至 C8 的前支與 T1 前支的大部分組成的軀體神經叢（圖 7.52）。神經叢起源於頸部，向外下越過 rib I 進入腋窩。

臂神經叢的各部分從內側到外側依次為：roots（根）、trunks（幹）、divisions（股） 與 cords（束）。所有支配上肢的主要神經都起源於臂神經叢，主要來自 cords。臂神經叢的近端部分在頸部位於 subclavian artery 後方，而更遠端部分圍繞 axillary artery。

臂神經叢的近端部分在頸部位於 subclavian artery 後方，而更遠端部分圍繞 axillary artery。

圖 7.45–7.52：腋窩的區域解剖學。圖 7.45 顯示後壁的通道；圖 7.46 為磁共振横切面影像；圖 7.47 為腋窩底的示意圖；圖 7.48 為通過腋窩的肌肉；圖 7.49 為腋动脉及其與 pectoralis minor 的關係；圖 7.50 為腋动脉的分支；圖 7.51 為腋靜脈；圖 7.52 為臂神經叢。

Head & Neck — Brachial Plexus & Axilla

Brachial Plexus（臂神經叢）

Roots（神經根）

The roots of the brachial plexus are the anterior rami of C5 to C8, and most of T1. Close to their origin, the roots receive gray rami communicantes from the sympathetic trunk (Fig. 7.52). These carry postganglionic sympathetic fibers onto the roots for distribution to the periphery. The roots and trunks enter the posterior triangle of the neck by passing between the anterior scalene and middle scalene muscles and lie superior and posterior to the subclavian artery.

Trunks（神經幹）

The three trunks of the brachial plexus originate from the roots, pass laterally over rib I, and enter the axilla (Fig. 7.52):

  • The superior trunk is formed by the union of C5 and C6 roots.
  • The middle trunk is a continuation of the C7 root.
  • The inferior trunk is formed by the union of the C8 and T1 roots.

The inferior trunk lies on rib I posterior to the subclavian artery; the middle and superior trunks are more superior in position.

Divisions（分支）

Each of the three trunks of the brachial plexus divides into an anterior and a posterior division (Fig. 7.52):

  • The three anterior divisions form parts of the brachial plexus that ultimately give rise to peripheral nerves associated with the anterior compartments of the arm and forearm.
  • The three posterior divisions combine to form parts of the brachial plexus that give rise to nerves associated with the posterior compartments.

臨床重點：No peripheral nerves originate directly from the divisions of the brachial plexus.

Cords（神經索）

The three cords of the brachial plexus originate from the divisions and are related to the second part of the axillary artery (Fig. 7.52):

  • The lateral cord results from the union of the anterior divisions of the upper and middle trunks and therefore has contributions from C5 to C7—it is positioned lateral to the second part of the axillary artery.
  • The medial cord is medial to the second part of the axillary artery and is the continuation of the anterior division of the inferior trunk—it contains contributions from C8 and T1.
  • The posterior cord occurs posterior to the second part of the axillary artery and originates as the union of all three posterior divisions—it contains contributions from all roots of the brachial plexus (C5 to T1).

臨床重點：Most of the major peripheral nerves of the upper limb originate from the cords of the brachial plexus. Generally, nerves associated with the anterior compartments of the upper limb arise from the medial and lateral cords, and nerves associated with the posterior compartments originate from the posterior cord.

Branches of the Brachial Plexus（臂神經叢的分支）

Branches of the Roots（神經根的分支）

In addition to small segmental branches from C5 to C8 to muscles of the neck and a contribution of C5 to the phrenic nerve, the roots of the brachial plexus give rise to the dorsal scapular nerve and long thoracic nerve (Fig. 7.53).

Dorsal Scapular Nerve（背肩胛神經）

The dorsal scapular nerve:

  • originates from the C5 root of the brachial plexus,
  • passes posteriorly, often piercing the middle scalene muscle in the neck, to reach and travel along the medial border of the scapula (Fig. 7.54), and
  • innervates the rhomboid major and rhomboid minor muscles from their deep surfaces.

Long Thoracic Nerve（胸長神經）

The long thoracic nerve:

  • originates from the anterior rami of C5 to C7,
  • passes vertically down the neck, through the axillary inlet, and down the medial wall of the axilla to supply the serratus anterior muscle (Fig. 7.54), and
  • lies on the superficial aspect of the serratus anterior muscle.

臨床重點：Damage to the long thoracic nerve results in “winged scapula” due to loss of serratus anterior function.

Branches of the Trunks（神經幹的分支）

The only branches from the trunks of the brachial plexus are two nerves that originate from the superior trunk (upper trunk): the suprascapular nerve and the nerve to the subclavius muscle (Fig. 7.53).

Suprascapular Nerve（肩胛上神經）

The suprascapular nerve (C5 and C6):

  • originates from the superior trunk of the brachial plexus,
  • passes laterally through the posterior triangle of the neck (Fig. 7.54) and through the suprascapular foramen to enter the posterior scapular region,
  • innervates the supraspinatus and infraspinatus muscles, and
  • is accompanied in the lateral parts of the neck and in the posterior scapular region by the suprascapular artery.

Nerve to the Subclavius Muscle（鎖骨下肌神經）

The nerve to the subclavius muscle (C5 and C6) is a small nerve that:

  • originates from the superior trunk of the brachial plexus,
  • passes anteroinferiorly over the subclavian artery and vein, and
  • innervates the subclavius muscle.

Branches of the Lateral Cord（外側索的分支）

Three nerves originate entirely or partly from the lateral cord (Fig. 7.53).

Lateral Pectoral Nerve（外側胸神經）

The lateral pectoral nerve is the most proximal of the branches from the lateral cord. It passes anteriorly, together with the thoraco-acromial artery, to penetrate the clavipectoral fascia that spans the gap between the subclavius and pectoralis minor muscles (Fig. 7.55), and innervates the pectoralis major muscle.

Musculocutaneous Nerve（肌皮神經）

The musculocutaneous nerve is a large terminal branch of the lateral cord. It passes laterally to penetrate the coracobrachialis muscle and pass between the biceps brachii and brachialis muscles in the arm, and innervates all three flexor muscles in the anterior compartment of the arm, terminating as the lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm.

Lateral Root of the Median Nerve（正中神經外側根）

The lateral root of the median nerve is the largest terminal branch of the lateral cord and passes medially to join a similar branch from the medial cord to form the median nerve (Fig. 7.55).

Branches of the Medial Cord（內側索的分支）

The medial cord has five branches (Fig. 7.55).

Medial Pectoral Nerve（內側胸神經）

The medial pectoral nerve is the most proximal branch. It receives a communicating branch from the lateral pectoral nerve and then passes anteriorly between the axillary artery and axillary vein. Branches of the nerve penetrate and supply the pectoralis minor muscle. Some of these branches pass through the muscle to reach and supply the pectoralis major muscle. Other branches occasionally pass around the inferior or lateral margin of the pectoralis minor muscle to reach the pectoralis major muscle.

Medial Cutaneous Nerve of the Arm（臂內側皮神經）

The medial cutaneous nerve of the arm (medial brachial cutaneous nerve) passes through the axilla and into the arm where it penetrates deep fascia and supplies skin over the medial side of the distal third of the arm. In the axilla, the nerve communicates with the intercostobrachial nerve of T2. Fibers of the medial cutaneous nerve of the arm innervate the upper part of the medial surface of the arm and floor of the axilla.

Medial Cutaneous Nerve of the Forearm（前臂內側皮神經）

The medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm (medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve) originates just distal to the origin of the medial cutaneous nerve of the arm. It passes out of the axilla and into the arm where it gives off a branch to the skin over the biceps brachii muscle, and then continues down the arm to penetrate the deep fascia with the basilic vein, continuing inferiorly to supply the skin over the anterior surface of the forearm. It innervates skin over the medial surface of the forearm down to the wrist.

Medial Root of the Median Nerve（正中神經內側根）

The medial root of the median nerve passes laterally to join with a similar root from the lateral cord to form the median nerve anterior to the third part of the axillary artery.

Ulnar Nerve（尺神經）

The ulnar nerve is a large terminal branch of the medial cord (Fig. 7.55). However, near its origin, it often receives a communicating branch from the lateral root of the median nerve originating from the lateral cord and carrying fibers from C7. The ulnar nerve passes through the arm and forearm into the hand where it innervates all intrinsic muscles of the hand (except for the three thenar muscles and the two lateral lumbrical muscles). On passing through the forearm, branches of the ulnar nerve innervate the flexor carpi ulnaris muscle and the medial half of the flexor digitorum profundus muscle. The ulnar nerve innervates skin over the palmar surface of the little finger, medial half of the ring finger, and associated palm and wrist, and the skin over the dorsal surface of the medial part of the hand.

Median Nerve（正中神經）

The median nerve is formed anterior to the third part of the axillary artery by the union of lateral and medial roots originating from the lateral and medial cords of the brachial plexus (Fig. 7.55). It passes into the arm anterior to the brachial artery and through the arm into the forearm, where branches innervate most of the muscles in the anterior compartment of the forearm (except for the flexor carpi ulnaris muscle and the medial half of the flexor digitorum profundus muscle, which are innervated by the ulnar nerve).

The median nerve continues into the hand to innervate:

  • the three thenar muscles associated with the thumb,
  • the two lateral lumbrical muscles associated with movement of the index and middle fingers, and
  • the skin over the palmar surface of the lateral three and one-half digits and over the lateral side of the palm and middle of the wrist.

臨床重點：The musculocutaneous nerve, the lateral root of the median nerve, the median nerve, the medial root of the median nerve, and the ulnar nerve form an M over the third part of the axillary artery. This feature, together with penetration of the coracobrachialis muscle by the musculocutaneous nerve, can be used to identify components of the brachial plexus in the axilla.

Branches of the Posterior Cord（後側索的分支）

Five nerves originate from the posterior cord of the brachial plexus:

  • the superior subscapular nerve,
  • the thoracodorsal nerve,
  • the inferior subscapular nerve,
  • the axillary nerve, and
  • the radial nerve (Fig. 7.53).

All these nerves except the radial nerve innervate muscles associated with the posterior wall of the axilla; the radial nerve passes into the arm and forearm.

Superior Subsscapular Nerve（上肩胛下神經）

The superior subscapular nerve is short and passes into and supplies the subscapularis muscle.

Thoracodorsal Nerve（胸背神經）

The thoracodorsal nerve is the longest of these three nerves and passes vertically along the posterior axillary wall. It penetrates and innervates the latissimus dorsi muscle.

Inferior Subsscapular Nerve（下肩胛下神經）

The inferior subscapular nerve also passes inferiorly along the posterior axillary wall and innervates the subscapularis and teres major muscles.

Axillary Nerve（腋神經）

The axillary nerve originates from the posterior cord and passes inferiorly and laterally along the posterior wall to exit the axilla through the quadrangular space (Fig. 7.56). It passes posteriorly around the surgical neck of the humerus and innervates both the deltoid and teres minor muscles. A superior lateral cutaneous nerve of the arm originates from the axillary nerve after passing through the quadrangular space and loops around the posterior margin of the deltoid muscle to innervate skin in that region. The axillary nerve is accompanied by the posterior circumflex humeral artery.

Radial Nerve（橈神經）

The radial nerve is the largest terminal branch of the posterior cord (Fig. 7.56). It passes out of the axilla and into the posterior compartment of the arm by passing through the triangular interval between the inferior border of the teres major muscle, the long head of the triceps brachii muscle, and the shaft of the humerus. It is accompanied through the triangular interval by the profunda brachii artery, which originates from the brachial artery in the anterior compartment of the arm.

The radial nerve and its branches innervate:

  • all muscles in the posterior compartments of the arm and forearm, and
  • the skin on the posterior aspect of the arm and forearm, the lower lateral surface of the arm, and the dorsal lateral surface of the hand.

The posterior cutaneous nerve of the arm (posterior brachial cutaneous nerve) originates from the radial nerve in the axilla and innervates skin on the posterior surface of the arm.

In the Clinic — Clinical Considerations（臨床重點）

Injuries to the Brachial Plexus（臂神經叢損傷）

臨床重點：The brachial plexus is an extremely complex structure. When damaged, it requires meticulous clinical history taking and examination. Assessment of the individual nerve functions can be obtained by nerve conduction studies and electromyography, which assess the latency of muscle contraction when the nerve is artificially stimulated.

臨床重點：Brachial plexus injuries are usually the result of blunt trauma producing nerve avulsions and disruption. These injuries are usually devastating for the function of the upper limb and require many months of dedicated rehabilitation for even a small amount of function to return.

臨床重點：Spinal cord injuries in the cervical region and direct pulling injuries tend to affect the roots of the brachial plexus. Severe trauma to the first rib usually affects the trunks. The divisions and cords of the brachial plexus can be injured by dislocation of the glenohumeral joint.

Axillary Lymphatics（腋淋巴系統）

All lymphatics from the upper limb drain into lymph nodes in the axilla (Fig. 7.57).

In addition, axillary nodes receive drainage from an extensive area on the adjacent trunk, which includes regions of the upper back and shoulder, the lower neck, the chest, and the upper anterolateral abdominal wall. Axillary nodes also receive drainage from approximately 75% of the mammary gland.

Axillary Lymph Nodes（腋淋巴結）

The 20–30 axillary nodes are generally divided into five groups on the basis of location:

  • Humeral (lateral) nodes: Posteromedial to the axillary vein, receive most of the lymphatic drainage from the upper limb.
  • Pectoral (anterior) nodes: Along the inferior margin of the pectoralis minor muscle along the course of the lateral thoracic vessels, receive drainage from the abdominal wall, the chest, and the mammary gland.
  • Subscapular (posterior) nodes: On the posterior axillary wall in association with the subscapular vessels, drain the posterior axillary wall and receive lymphatics from the back, the shoulder, and the neck.
  • Central nodes: Embedded in axillary fat, receive tributaries from humeral, subscapular, and pectoral groups of nodes.
  • Apical nodes: The most superior group of nodes in the axilla, drain all other groups of nodes in the region. In addition, they receive lymphatic vessels that accompany the cephalic vein as well as vessels that drain the superior region of the mammary gland.

臨床重點：Efferent vessels from the apical group converge to form the subclavian trunk, which usually joins the venous system at the junction between the right subclavian vein and the right internal jugular vein in the neck. On the left, the subclavian trunk usually joins the thoracic duct in the base of the neck.

Breast Cancer（乳癌）

臨床重點：Lymphatic drainage from the lateral part of the breast passes through nodes in the axilla. Significant disruption to the normal lymphatic drainage of the upper limb may occur if a mastectomy or a surgical axillary nodal clearance has been carried out for breast cancer. Furthermore, some patients have radiotherapy to the axilla to prevent the spread of metastatic disease, but a side effect of this is the destruction of the tiny lymphatics as well as the cancer cells.

臨床重點：If the lymphatic drainage of the upper limb is damaged, the arm may swell and pitting edema (lymphedema) may develop.

Axillary Process of the Mammary Gland（乳腺腋突）

Although the mammary gland is in superficial fascia overlying the thoracic wall, its superolateral region extends along the inferior margin of the pectoralis major muscle toward the axilla. In some cases, this may pass around the margin of the muscle to penetrate deep fascia and enter the axilla (Fig. 7.58). This axillary process rarely reaches as high as the apex of the axilla.

Gray’s Anatomy — Head & Neck

Upper Limb — ARM（臂部）

概述

臂部（Arm） 是介於**肩部（shoulder）與肘部（elbow）之間的上肢區域（圖 7.59）。臂部上方經內側與腋窩（axilla）相通。下方的肘窩（cubital fossa）是許多重要結構由臂部通往前臂的通道，位於肘關節（elbow joint）**前方。

臂部由**內側肌間隔（medial intermuscular septum）與外側肌間隔（lateral intermuscular septum）分隔為兩個腔室，這些肌間隔從肱骨（humerus）**兩側延伸至包覆肢體的深筋膜（圖 7.59）。

  • 前腔室（Anterior compartment）：主要含屈肌，負責屈肘關節
  • 後腔室（Posterior compartment）：含伸肌，負責伸肘關節

主要神經與血管供應並穿行於各腔室。

臨床重點：臂部兩個腔室的分隔結構具有臨床意義，例如前臂腔室症候群（compartment syndrome）可能發生於單一腔室，需精確區分受影響部位。

骨骼（Bones）

臂部的骨骼支撐為肱骨（humerus）（圖 7.60）。臂部多數大型肌肉均附著於前臂兩骨——**橈骨（radius）與尺骨（ulna）**的近端，負責在肘關節處屈伸前臂。此外，主要分布於前臂、支配手部運動的肌肉，則起源於肱骨遠端。

肱骨幹與遠端

從橫切面看，肱骨幹呈三角形，具有：

  • 前緣（anterior border）、外側緣（lateral border）、內側緣（medial border）
  • 前外側面（anterolateral surface）、前內側面（anteromedial surface）、後面（posterior surface）（圖 7.60）

後面上方有一線性粗糙區域，為肱三頭肌外側頭（lateral head of triceps brachii）的附著處，該附著處始於外科頸（surgical neck）下方，斜向延伸至三角肌粗隆（deltoid tuberosity）。

臨床重點：肱骨外科頸骨折常伴隨**腋神經（axillary nerve）**損傷，因神經繞過外科頸後方行走於肩關節周圍。

後面中部及前外側面相鄰區域有淺橈神經溝（radial groove），斜向通過骨頭，與三角肌粗隆後緣平行。**橈神經（radial nerve）與肱深動脈（profunda brachii artery）**行走於此溝中。

約在骨幹中段，內側緣有一細長粗糙區域，為**喙肱肌（coracobrachialis）**附著處。

分隔前、後腔室的內、外側肌間隔，分別附著於內側緣與外側緣（圖 7.61）。

遠端：骨頭變扁平，這些骨緣擴展為外側髁上嵴（lateral supraepicondylar ridge）與內側髁上嵴（medial supraepicondylar ridge）。外側髁上嵴較內側嵴更明顯，粗糙區域為前臂後腔室肌肉的附著處。

肱骨遠端呈扁平狀（前後向），具有髁（condyle）、兩個髁上突（epicondyle）及三個窩（fossa）（圖 7.61）。

髁（Condyle）

髁的兩個關節部分——肱骨小頭（capitulum）與滑車（trochlea）——與前臂兩骨形成關節：

  • Capitulum（肱骨小頭）：與前臂橈骨關節。位於外側，呈半球形，向前並略向下突出。從肱骨後方觀察時不可見。
  • Trochlea（滑車）：與前臂尺骨關節。 Pulley 形狀，位於 capitulum 內側。內側緣較外側緣更突出，與 capitulum 不同的是，它延伸至骨頭後面。
兩個髁上突（Epicondyles）

兩個髁上突緊鄰並略上位於 trochlea 與 capitulum 上方（圖 7.61）。

  • 內側髁上突（Medial epicondyle）：大型骨性突起，是肘內側主要可觸及的標誌，從肱骨遠端向內側突出。表面有大橢圓形壓跡，為前臂前腔室肌肉的附著處。**尺神經（ulnar nerve）**從臂部進入前臂，繞過內側髁上突後方，可在此處觸及其緊贴骨頭的走向。

臨床重點：尺神經在內側髁上突後方的通道是臨床上重要的解剖位置。尺神經炎（ulnar neuritis）或肘部尺神經卡壓（cubital tunnel syndrome）常在此區域發生，表現為手部感覺異常及精細動作障礙。

  • 外側髁上突（ Lateral epicondyle）：比內側髁上突小很多。位於 capitulum 外側，有不規則大壓跡，為前臂後腔室肌肉的附著處。
三個窩（Fossae）

三個窩位於 trochlea 與 capitulum 上方的肱骨遠端（圖 7.61）。

  • 橈骨窩（Radial fossa）：三窩中最不明顯，位於肱骨前面、capitulum 正上方。
  • 冠狀窩（Coronoid fossa）：緊鄰 radial fossa，位於 trochlea 上方。
  • 鷹嘴窩（Olecranon fossa）：三窩中最大，位於肱骨遠端後面、trochlea 正上方。

三窩在肘關節運動時容納前臂骨的突起。

橈骨近端（Proximal end of the radius）

橈骨近端由頭（head）、**頸（neck）與橈骨粗隆（radial tuberosity）**組成（圖 7.62A,B）。

  • 橈骨頭（Head of radius）：厚盤狀結構，位於水平面。圓形上面凹陷，與肱骨 capitulum 形成關節。厚邊緣在內側寬闊，與尺骨近端**橈骨切跡（radial notch）**形成關節。
  • 橈骨頸（ Neck of radius）：頭與骨幹上 radial tuberosity 之間的短窄圓柱狀骨。
  • 橈骨粗隆（Radial tuberosity）：橈骨內側面的高大鈍性突起，緊鄰頸下方。大部分表面粗糙，為**肱二頭肌腱（biceps brachii tendon）**附著處。**橈骨斜線（oblique line of radius）**從 radial tuberosity 下緣斜向延伸穿過骨幹。

尺骨近端（Proximal end of the ulna）

尺骨近端遠比橈骨近端大，由鷹嘴（olecranon）、冠狀突（coronoid process）、滑車切跡（trochlear notch）、**橈骨切跡（radial notch）與尺骨粗隆（tuberosity of the ulna）**組成（圖 7.63A,B）。

  • Olecranon（鷹嘴）：大型骨性突起，從尺骨向上延伸。前外側面為關節面，參與構成與肱骨滑車關節的 trochlear notch。上面有大粗糙壓跡，為**肱三頭肌（triceps brachii）**附著處。後面光滑，略呈三角形，可觸及為「肘尖」。
  • 冠狀突（Coronoid process）：從尺骨近端向前突出（圖 7.63）。其上前外側面為關節面，與 olecranon 共同構成滑車切跡。外側面有橈骨切跡與橈骨頭形成關節。
  • 緊鄰 radial notch 下方有一窩，允許 radial tuberosity 在旋前與旋後時改變位置。此窩後緣擴展形成旋後肌嵴（supinator crest）。冠狀突前面呈三角形，尖端指向遠端，有多個肌肉附著粗糙區。最大粗糙區位於前面尖端的尺骨粗隆，是**肱肌（brachialis）**的附著點。

肌肉（Muscles）

前腔室（Anterior Compartment）

臂部前腔室含三塊肌肉——Coracobrachialis（喙肱肌）、Brachialis（肱肌）與Biceps brachii（肱二頭肌），主要由**肌皮神經（musculocutaneous nerve）**支配。

Coracobrachialis（喙肱肌）

Coracobrachialis 從肩胛骨**喙突（coracoid process）**尖端延伸至肱骨幹中段內側（圖 7.64 及表 7.8）。它穿過腋窩，被肌皮神經穿過並支配。

功能：屈臂（Flexes the arm）。

Biceps brachii（肱二頭肌）

Biceps brachii 有兩個頭：

  • 短頭（Short head）：與 coracobrachialis 共同起源於 coracoid process。
  • 長頭（Long head）：以肌腱起源於肩胛骨的盂上結節（supraglenoid tubercle）（圖 7.64 及表 7.8）。

長頭肌腱穿過盂肱關節（glenohumeral joint），位於肱骨頭上方，隨後穿過**結節間溝（intertubercular sulcus）**進入臂部。在臂部，肌腱與肌肉會合，與短頭的肌肉一起覆蓋於 brachialis 上。

兩頭會合形成單一肌腱，附著於橈骨粗隆（radial tuberosity）。當肌腱進入前臂時，從內側展開一片扁平結締組織（二頭肌腱膜（bicipital aponeurosis）），融入覆蓋前臂前腔室的深筋膜。

功能：

  • 強力的前臂屈肌（在肘關節處）
  • 當肘關節屈曲時，最有力的前臂旋後肌
  • 因為兩個頭都跨越盂肱關節，亦可屈肩關節

臨床重點：臨床上，叩擊肘部的肱二頭肌腱用於測試主要是**脊髓第6節段（C6）**的功能完整性。

Brachialis（肱肌）：起源於肱骨前面遠端一半及相鄰的肌間隔（特別是內側）（圖 7.64 及表 7.8）。位於 biceps brachii 深面，腹背扁平，匯聚成肌腱附著於尺骨粗隆。

功能：屈前臂（在肘關節處）。

支配：主要由肌皮神經支配。外側小部分由橈神經支配。

臨床重點：二頭肌腱rupture（斷裂）

上肢肌肉與肌腱的斷裂並不常見，但最常斷裂的肌腱是肱二頭肌長頭腱。單獨發生時對上肢功能影響不大，但會產生特徵性畸形——屈肘時肌肉腹部異常突出，稱為「Popeye 徵象」。

總表：前臂腔室肌肉（表 7.8）

Coracobrachialis Coracoid process 尖端 肱骨幹中段線性粗糙區 Musculocutaneous nerve (C5, C6, C7) 屈肩關節
Biceps brachii 長頭：Scapula 盂上結節；短頭：Coracoid process 尖端 Radial tuberosity Musculocutaneous nerve (C5, C6) 強力的前臂屈肌與旋後肌；輔助屈肩關節

後腔室（Posterior Compartment）

臂部後腔室唯一的肌肉是Triceps brachii（肱三頭肌）（圖 7.65 及表 7.9），由**橈神經（radial nerve）**支配。

Triceps brachii 有三個頭：

  • 長頭（Long head）：起源於肩胛骨盂下結節（infraglenoid tubercle）
  • 內側頭（Medial head）：起源於肱骨幹後面、橈神經溝下方的大範圍區域
  • 外側頭（Lateral head）：起源於肱骨橈神經溝上方線性粗糙區

三頭會合形成粗大肌腱，附著於尺骨olecranon 上方。

功能：伸前臂（在肘關節處）。長頭亦可伸並內收肩關節。

臨床重點：臨床上，叩擊肱三頭肌腱用於測試主要是**脊髓第7節段（C7）**的功能完整性。

總表：後臂腔室肌肉（表 7.9）
肌肉 起源 附著 神經支配 功能
Triceps brachii 長頭：Scapula 盂下結節；內側頭：肱骨後面；外側頭：肱骨後面 Olecranon Radial nerve (C6, C7, C8) 伸前臂（在肘關節處）；長頭亦可伸並內收肩關節

動靜脈（Arteries and Veins）

臂动脉（Brachial Artery）

臂部主要动脉——Brachial artery（臂动脉）位於前腔室（圖 7.66A）。在大圓肌（teres major）下緣延續腋动脉（axillary artery），於肘關節遠端分為橈动脉（radial artery）與尺动脉（ulnar artery）。

近端臂部，臂动脉位於內側。遠端臂部，它移向外側，位於肱骨外側髁上突與內側髁上突之間的中點。它越過肘關節前方，位於肱二頭肌腱的內側。臂动脉全程可觸及。近端可將其壓向肱骨內側以止血。

臂动脉在臂部的分支包括：

  • 鄰近肌肉的分支
  • 兩個尺側副血管（ulnar collateral vessels），參與肘關節周圍动脉網絡（圖 7.66B）
  • 肱深动脉（Profunda brachii artery）——營養肱骨的血管，穿過骨幹前內側面孔

臨床重點：臂动脉是上肢主要的搏動性止血點。在創傷或手術中，可於臂部中段將臂动脉壓向肱骨以控制出血。

肱深动脉（Profunda Brachii Artery）

Profunda brachii artery 是臂动脉最大的分支，進入並供應臂部後腔室（圖 7.66A,B）。它與橈神經一起進入後腔室，兩者穿過三角間隙（triangular interval）——由肱骨幹、大圓肌下緣與長頭外側緣構成。隨後沿肱骨後面橈神經溝行走，位於肱三頭肌外側頭深面。

分支供應鄰近肌肉，並與**旋肱後动脉（posterior circumflex humeral artery）**吻合。最終分為兩條側支，參與肘關節周圍动脉吻合網絡（圖 7.66B）。

臨床重點：血壓測量

血壓是極重要的生理參數。高血壓（高血壓病）需治療以預防長期併發症如中風。低血壓可由嚴重失血、廣泛感染或心輸出不良（如心肌梗塞後）引起。

多數臨床醫師使用血壓計（sphygmomanometer）與聽診器測量血壓。血壓計的壓脈帶纏繞臂部中段，壓迫臂动脉向肱骨。壓脈帶充氣使壓力超過收縮壓（大於 120 mm Hg）。醫師將聽診器置於肘窩的臂动脉上聆聽脈搏。當血壓計壓力降至收縮壓以下時，脈搏變為可聽到的規律敲擊聲。當壓力繼續下降至舒張壓以下時，敲擊聲消失。正常範圍為 120/80 mm Hg（收縮壓/舒張壓）。

靜脈（Veins）

成對的**臂靜脈（brachial veins）**沿臂动脉內外側行走，接受伴隨动脉分支的靜脈屬支（圖 7.67）。

此外，臂部還有兩條大型皮下靜脈——Basilic vein（貴要靜脈）與Cephalic vein（頭靜脈）。

  • Basilic vein（貴要靜脈）：垂直行走於臂部遠端一半，穿過深筋膜位於臂动脉內側，於大圓肌下緣成為腋靜脈（axillary vein）。臂靜脈匯入貴要靜脈或腋靜脈。
  • Cephalic vein（頭靜脈）：沿臂部前外側向上行走，穿過腋窩前壁匯入腋靜脈。
