臨床重點摘要

  • 內側髁上突是臨床上可觸及的重要解剖標誌，尺神經繞過其後方行走
  • 橈神經在橈神經溝行走，骨折或長期壓迫可造成損傷
  • 臂动脉在臂部中段可觸及並壓迫止血
  • 血壓測量使用血壓計與聽診器，正常值 120/80 mm Hg
  • 二頭肌長頭腱斷裂產生特徵性「Popeye 徵象」

Gray’s Anatomy — Upper Limb: Arm, Elbow & Forearm

上臂的神經（Nerves of the Arm）

Musculocutaneous Nerve

The musculocutaneous nerve leaves the axilla and enters the arm by passing through the coracobrachialis muscle (Fig. 7.68). It passes diagonally down the arm in the plane between the biceps brachii and brachialis muscles. After giving rise to motor branches in the arm, it emerges laterally to the tendon of the biceps brachii muscle at the elbow, penetrates deep fascia, and continues as the lateral cutaneous nerve of forearm.

The musculocutaneous nerve provides:

  • Motor innervation to all muscles in the anterior compartment of the arm
  • Sensory innervation to skin on the lateral surface of the forearm

臨床重點：Musculocutaneous nerve injury is uncommon due to its relatively protected position. When injured, patients lose elbow flexion (biceps brachii, brachialis) and have numbness over the lateral forearm.

Median Nerve

The median nerve enters the arm from the axilla at the inferior margin of the teres major muscle (Fig. 7.68). It passes vertically down the medial side of the arm in the anterior compartment and is related to the brachial artery throughout its course:

  • In proximal regions, the median nerve is immediately lateral to the brachial artery.
  • In more distal regions, the median nerve crosses to the medial side of the brachial artery and lies anterior to the elbow joint.

The median nerve has no major branches in the arm, but a branch to the pronator teres muscle may originate immediately proximal to the elbow joint.

Ulnar Nerve

The ulnar nerve enters the arm with the median nerve and axillary artery (Fig. 7.68). It passes through proximal regions medial to the axillary artery. In the middle of the arm, the ulnar nerve penetrates the medial intermuscular septum and enters the posterior compartment where it lies anterior to the medial head of the triceps brachii muscle. It passes posterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus and then into the anterior compartment of the forearm.

The ulnar nerve has no major branches in the arm.

Radial Nerve

The radial nerve originates from the posterior cord of the brachial plexus and enters the arm by crossing the inferior margin of the teres major muscle (Fig. 7.69). As it enters the arm, it lies posterior to the brachial artery. Accompanied by the profunda brachii artery, the radial nerve enters the posterior compartment of the arm by passing through the triangular interval.

As the radial nerve passes diagonally, from medial to lateral, through the posterior compartment, it lies in the radial groove directly on bone. On the lateral side of the arm, it passes anteriorly through the lateral intermuscular septum and enters the anterior compartment where it lies between the brachialis muscle and the brachioradialis muscle, which attaches to the lateral supraepicondylar ridge of the humerus. The radial nerve enters the forearm anterior to the lateral epicondyle of the humerus, just deep to the brachioradialis muscle.

In the arm, the radial nerve has muscular and cutaneous branches (Fig. 7.69):

  • Muscular branches include those to the triceps brachii, brachioradialis, and extensor carpi radialis longus muscles. In addition, the radial nerve contributes to the innervation of the lateral part of the brachialis muscle. One of the branches to the medial head of the triceps brachii muscle arises before the radial nerve’s entrance into the posterior compartment and passes vertically down the arm in association with the ulnar nerve.
  • Cutaneous branches of the radial nerve that originate in the posterior compartment of the arm are the inferior lateral cutaneous nerve of the arm and the posterior cutaneous nerve of the forearm, both of which penetrate through the lateral head of the triceps brachii muscle and the overlying deep fascia to become subcutaneous.

臨床重點：Radial nerve injury in the arm — The radial nerve is tightly bound with the profunda brachii artery between the medial and lateral heads of the triceps brachii muscle in the radial groove. If the humerus is fractured, the radial nerve may become stretched or transected in this region, leading to permanent damage and loss of function. This injury is typical and the nerve should always be tested when a fracture of the midshaft of the humerus is suspected. The patient’s symptoms usually include wrist drop (due to denervation of the extensor muscles) and sensory changes over the dorsum of the hand.

臨床重點：Median nerve injury in the arm — In the arm and forearm the median nerve is usually not injured by trauma because of its relatively deep position. The commonest neurological problem associated with the median nerve is compression beneath the flexor retinaculum at the wrist (carpal tunnel syndrome). On very rare occasions, a fibrous band may arise from the anterior aspect of the humerus beneath which the median nerve passes. This is an embryological remnant of the coracobrachialis muscle and is sometimes called the ligament of Struthers; occasionally, it may calcify. This band can compress the median nerve, resulting in weakness of the flexor muscles in the forearm and the thenar muscles. Nerve conduction studies will demonstrate the site of nerve compression.

肘關節（Elbow Joint）

The elbow joint is a complex joint involving three separate articulations, which share a common synovial cavity (Fig. 7.71):

  • The joints between the trochlear notch of the ulna and the trochlea of the humerus and between the head of the radius and the capitulum of the humerus are primarily involved with hinge-like flexion and extension of the forearm on the arm and, together, are the principal articulations of the elbow joint.
  • The joint between the head of the radius and the radial notch of the ulna, the proximal radio-ulnar joint, is involved with pronation and supination of the forearm.

The articular surfaces of the bones are covered with hyaline cartilage.

Synovial Membrane

The synovial membrane originates from the edges of the articular cartilage and lines the radial fossa, the coronoid fossa, the olecranon fossa, the deep surface of the joint capsule, and the medial surface of the trochlea (Fig. 7.72).

The synovial membrane is separated from the fibrous membrane of the joint capsule by pads of fat in regions overlying the coronoid fossa, the olecranon fossa, and the radial fossa. These fat pads accommodate the related bony processes during extension and flexion of the elbow. Attachments of the brachialis and triceps brachii muscles to the joint capsule overlying these regions pull the attached fat pads out of the way when the adjacent bony processes are moved into the fossae.

Joint Capsule and Ligaments

The fibrous membrane of the joint capsule overlies the synovial membrane, encloses the joint, and attaches to the medial epicondyle and the margins of the olecranon, coronoid, and radial fossae of the humerus (Fig. 7.73). It also attaches to the coronoid process and olecranon of the ulna. On the lateral side, the free inferior margin of the joint capsule passes around the neck of the radius from an anterior attachment to the coronoid process of the ulna to a posterior attachment to the base of the olecranon.

The fibrous membrane of the joint capsule is thickened medially and laterally to form collateral ligaments, which support the flexion and extension movements of the elbow joint (Fig. 7.73):

  • Ulnar collateral ligament (medial)
  • Radial collateral ligament (lateral)

In addition, the external surface of the joint capsule is reinforced laterally where it cuffs the head of the radius with a strong anular ligament of the radius. Although this ligament blends with the fibrous membrane of the joint capsule in most regions, they are separate posteriorly. The anular ligament of the radius also blends with the radial collateral ligament.

The anular ligament of the radius and related joint capsule allow the radial head to slide against the radial notch of the ulna and pivot on the capitulum during pronation and supination.

The deep surface of the fibrous membrane of the joint capsule and the related anular ligament of the radius that articulate with the sides of the radial head are lined by cartilage. A pocket of synovial membrane (sacciform recess) protrudes from the inferior free margin of the joint capsule and facilitates rotation of the radial head during pronation and supination.

Vascular Supply and Innervation

  • Vascular supply: through an anastomotic network of vessels derived from collateral and recurrent branches of the brachial, profunda brachii, radial, and ulnar arteries.
  • Innervation: predominantly by branches of the radial and musculocutaneous nerves, but there may be some innervation by branches of the ulnar and median nerves.

臨床重點：Supracondylar fracture of the humerus — Elbow injuries in children may result in a transverse fracture of the distal end of the humerus, above the level of the epicondyles. This fracture is termed a supracondylar fracture. The distal fragment and its soft tissues are pulled posteriorly by the triceps muscle. This posterior displacement effectively “bowstrings” the brachial artery over the irregular proximal fracture fragment. In children, this is a relatively devastating injury: the muscles of the anterior compartment of the forearm are rendered ischemic and form severe contractions, significantly reducing the function of the anterior compartment and flexor muscles (Volkmann’s ischemic contracture).

臨床重點：Pulled elbow — Pulled elbow is a disorder that typically occurs in children under 5 years of age. It is commonly caused by a sharp pull of the child’s hand, usually when the child is pulled up a curb. The not-yet-developed head of the radius and the laxity of the anular ligament of the radius allow the head to sublux from this cuff of tissue. Pulled elbow is extremely painful, but can be treated easily by simple supination and compression of the elbow joint by the clinician. When the radial head is relocated the pain subsides immediately and the child can continue with normal activity.

臨床重點：Developmental changes in the elbow joint — The elbow joint can be injured in many ways; the types of injuries are age dependent. When a fracture or soft tissue trauma is suspected, a plain lateral and an anteroposterior radiograph are obtained. In an adult it is usually not difficult to interpret the radiograph, but in children additional factors require interpretation. As the elbow develops in children, numerous secondary ossification centers appear before and around puberty. It is easy to mistakenly interpret these as fractures. In addition, it is also possible for the epiphyses and apophyses to be “pulled off” or disrupted. Therefore, when interpreting a child’s radiograph of the elbow, the physician must know the child’s age. Fusion occurs at around the time of puberty. An understanding of the normal epiphyses and apophyses and their normal relationship to the bones will secure a correct diagnosis. The approximate ages of appearance of the secondary ossification centers around the elbow joint are:

  • Capitulum — 1 year
  • Head of radius — 5 years
  • Medial epicondyle — 5 years
  • Trochlea — 11 years
  • Olecranon — 12 years
  • Lateral epicondyle — 13 years

臨床重點：Fracture of the head of the radius — A fracture of the head of the radius is a common injury and can cause appreciable morbidity. It is one of the typical injuries that occur with a fall on the outstretched hand. On falling, the force is transmitted to the radial head, which fractures. These fractures typically result in loss of full extension, and potential surgical reconstruction may require long periods of physiotherapy to obtain a full range of movement at the elbow joint. A lateral radiograph of a fracture of the head of the radius typically demonstrates the secondary phenomenon of this injury. When the bone is fractured, fluid fills the synovial cavity, elevating the small pad of fat within the coronoid and olecranon fossae. These fat pads appear as areas of lucency on the lateral radiograph — the “fat pad” sign. This radiological finding is useful because fracture of the head of the radius is not always clearly visible. If there is an appropriate clinical history, tenderness around the head of the radius, and a positive fat pad sign, a fracture can be inferred clinically even if no fracture can be identified on the radiograph.

臨床重點：“Tennis” and “golfer’s” elbow (epicondylitis) — It is not uncommon for people who are involved in sports such as golf and tennis to develop an overuse strain of the origins of the flexor and extensor muscles of the forearm. The pain is typically around the epicondyles and usually resolves after rest. If pain and inflammation persist, surgical division of the extensor or flexor origin from the bone may be necessary. Typically, in tennis players this pain occurs on the lateral epicondyle and common extensor origin (tennis elbow), whereas in golfers it occurs on the medial epicondyle and common flexor origin (golfer’s elbow).

臨床重點：Elbow arthritis — Osteoarthritis is extremely common and is usually most severe in the dominant limb. From time to time an arthritic elbow may undergo such degenerative change that small bone fragments appear in the articular cavity. Given the relatively small joint space, these fragments can result in an appreciable reduction in flexion and extension, and typically lodge within the olecranon and coronoid fossae.

臨床重點：Ulnar nerve injury at the elbow — Posterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus the ulnar nerve is bound in a fibro-osseous tunnel (the cubital tunnel) by a retinaculum. Older patients may develop degenerative changes within this tunnel, which compresses the ulnar nerve when flexed. The repeated action of flexion and extension of the elbow may cause local nerve damage, resulting in impaired function of the ulnar nerve. Accessory muscles and localized neuritis in this region secondary to direct trauma may also produce ulnar nerve damage.

肘窩（Cubital Fossa）

The cubital fossa is an important area of transition between the arm and the forearm. It is located anterior to the elbow joint and is a triangular depression formed between two forearm muscles:

  • The brachioradialis muscle originating from the lateral supra-epicondylar ridge of the humerus
  • The pronator teres muscle originating from the medial epicondyle of the humerus (Fig. 7.75A)

The base of the triangle is an imaginary horizontal line between the medial and lateral epicondyles. The bed or floor of the fossa is formed mainly by the brachialis muscle.

Major Contents of the Cubital Fossa

From lateral to medial, the major contents are:

  1. Tendon of the biceps brachii muscle
  2. Brachial artery
  3. Median nerve (Fig. 7.75B)

The brachial artery normally bifurcates into the radial and ulnar arteries in the apex of the fossa (Fig. 7.75B), although this bifurcation may occur much higher in the arm, even in the axilla. When taking a blood pressure reading from a patient, the clinician places the stethoscope over the brachial artery in the cubital fossa.

The median nerve lies immediately medial to the brachial artery and leaves the fossa by passing between the ulnar and humeral heads of the pronator teres muscle (Fig. 7.75C).

The brachial artery and the median nerve are covered and protected anteriorly in the distal part of the cubital fossa by the bicipital aponeurosis (Fig. 7.75B). This flat connective tissue membrane passes between the medial side of the tendon of the biceps brachii muscle and deep fascia of the forearm.

Radial Nerve in the Cubital Fossa

The radial nerve lies just under the lip of the brachioradialis muscle, which forms the lateral margin of the fossa (Fig. 7.75C). In this position, the radial nerve divides into:

  • Superficial branch: continues into the forearm just deep to the brachioradialis muscle
  • Deep branch: passes between the two heads of the supinator muscle to access the posterior compartment of the forearm

臨床重點：Construction of a dialysis fistula — Many patients throughout the world require renal dialysis for kidney failure. The patient’s blood is filtered and cleaned by the dialysis machine. Blood therefore has to be taken from patients into the filtering device and then returned to them. This process of dialysis occurs over many hours and requires considerable flow rates of 250–500 ml per minute. To enable such large volumes of blood to be removed from and returned to the body, the blood is taken from vessels that have a high flow. As no veins in the peripheral limbs have such high flow, a surgical procedure is necessary to create such a system. In most patients, the radial artery is anastomosed (joined) to the cephalic vein at the wrist, or the brachial artery is anastomosed to the cephalic vein at the elbow. After six weeks, the veins increase in size in response to their arterial blood flow and are amenable to direct cannulation for dialysis.

Roof of the Cubital Fossa

The roof of the cubital fossa is formed by superficial fascia and skin. The most important structure within the roof is the median cubital vein (Fig. 7.75D), which passes diagonally across the roof and connects the cephalic vein on the lateral side of the upper limb with the basilic vein on the medial side. The bicipital aponeurosis separates the median cubital vein from the brachial artery and median nerve.

Other structures within the roof are cutaneous nerves — the medial cutaneous and lateral cutaneous nerves of the forearm.

The ulnar nerve does not pass through the cubital fossa. Instead, it passes posterior to the medial epicondyle.

前臂（Forearm）

The forearm is the part of the upper limb that extends between the elbow joint and the wrist joint. Proximally, most major structures pass between the arm and forearm through, or in relation to, the cubital fossa, which is anterior to the elbow joint (Fig. 7.77). The exception is the ulnar nerve, which passes posterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus.

Distally, structures pass between the forearm and the hand through, or anterior to, the carpal tunnel (Fig. 7.77). The major exception is the radial artery, which passes dorsally around the wrist to enter the hand posteriorly.

Compartments of the Forearm

The forearm is divided into:

  • Anterior compartment — contains flexor muscles, median and ulnar nerves, and brachial artery
  • Posterior compartment — contains extensor muscles, radial nerve, and posterior interosseous vessels

The two compartments are separated by the interosseous membrane, the lateral intermuscular septum, and the deep fascia.

臨床重點：Compartment syndromes — Fractures of the forearm bones or supracondylar fractures can lead to increased pressure within the anterior or posterior compartments. This can compromise blood flow and nerve function, leading to Volkmann’s ischemic contracture if not treated promptly. Clinical signs include pain with passive stretch, swelling, and eventual neurological deficits.

Head & Neck — Gray’s Anatomy Segment 8

Forearm Bones & Joints

前臂的骨骼框架由兩塊平行骨組成：radius（橈骨） 和 ulna（尺骨）。Radius 位於外側，近端較細，與肱骨形成關節；遠端較寬，與腕骨形成腕關節。Ulna 位於內側，其近端和遠端的尺寸與 radius 相反：近端粗大，遠端細小。Radius 和 ulna 之間的近端和遠端關節允許 radius 遠端繞著 ulna 滑動，產生手掌的**pronation（旋前）**和 supination（旋後）。

與手臂一樣，前臂分為前側 compartment（肌室）和後側 compartment（肌室）。這些 compartments 由以下結構分開：

  • lateral intermuscular septum（外側肌間隔）：從 radius 前緣延伸至肢體深層筋膜
  • interosseous membrane（骨間膜）：連接 radius 和 ulna 沿大部分長度的相鄰邊界
  • 深層筋膜沿 ulna 後緣的附著

Radius（橈骨）— 骨幹與遠端

Radius 的骨幹近端狹窄，與 radial tuberosity 和頸部連續；遠端則明顯寬闊。

在大部分長度中，radius 骨幹呈三角形橫切面，具有：

  • 三條邊界（borders）：anterior border、posterior border、interosseous border
  • 三個面（surfaces）：anterior surface、posterior surface、lateral surface

Anterior border 起於骨骼內側的 radial tuberosity 延續。在骨骼的上三分之一處，它作為 radius 的 oblique line（斜線） 從內側斜向穿過骨幹至外側。Posterior border 僅在骨幹中三分之一處明顯。Interosseous border 銳利，是 interosseous membrane（骨間膜） 的附著處，連接 radius 和 ulna。

Radius 的 anterior surface 和 posterior surface 通常光滑，而 lateral surface 大約中段有一個橢圓形粗糙區，用於 pronator teres 的附著。

從前方看，radius 的遠端寬闊且前後扁平。因此，radius 具有寬大的 anterior 和 posterior surfaces，以及狹窄的 medial 和 lateral surfaces。Posterior surface 的特徵是存在一個大型 dorsal tubercle（背側結節），作為拇指伸肌之一（extensor pollicis longus）的滑輪。Medial surface 有與 ulna 遠端關節的明顯關節面。Lateral surface 呈菱形，向遠端延伸為 radial styloid process（橈骨莖突）。

骨骼遠端有兩個關節面，與兩塊腕骨（scaphoid 和 lunate）關節。

Ulna（尺骨）— 骨幹與遠端

Ulna 的骨幹上部寬闊，與較大的近端連續；下部狹窄，形成較小的遠端頭部。與 radius 一樣，ulna 骨幹呈三角形橫切面，具有：

  • 三條邊界（borders）：anterior border、posterior border、interosseous border
  • 三個面（surfaces）：anterior surface、posterior surface、medial surface

Anterior border 光滑且圓鈍。Posterior border 銳利且沿整個長度可觸及。Interosseous border 同樣銳利，是 interosseous membrane 的附著處，連接 ulna 和 radius。

Ulna 的 anterior surface 光滑，但在遠端有明顯的線性粗糙區，用於 pronator quadratus 肌肉的附著。Medial surface 光滑且無明顯特徵。Posterior surface 有線條，分隔不同的肌肉附著區域。

Ulna 的遠端較小，其特徵為圓形的**頭部（head）**和 ulnar styloid process（尺骨莖突）。頭部的 anterolateral 和遠端部分覆蓋有關節軟骨。Ulnar styloid process 起於 ulna 的 posteromedial 方面，向遠端突出。

臨床重點：橈骨與尺骨骨折

Radius 和 ulna 近端透過複雜的韌帶系列附著於肱骨，遠端附著於腕骨。雖然骨骼是分开的，但它們作為一個整體功能。當前臂發生嚴重損傷時，通常涉及兩塊骨骼，導致兩骨骨折或更常見的是一骨骨折伴另一骨脫臼。

有三種經典的前臂損傷：

  • Monteggia’s fracture（Monteggia 骨折）：ulna 近端三分之一骨折，合併 radius 頭部在肘部的前方脫臼
  • Galeazzi’s fracture（Galeazzi 骨折）：radius 遠端三分之一骨折，合併手腕處 ulna 頭部的半脫臼（subluxation）
  • Colles’ fracture（Colles 骨折）：radius 遠端骨折，合併向後移位

任何 radius 或 ulna 骨折都應拍攝肘部和手腕的額外影像，以排除脫臼。

Distal Radio-Ulnar Joint（遠端橈尺關節）

遠端 radio-ulnar 關節位於 ulna 頭部的關節面、radius 末端的 ulnar notch（尺骨切跡） 以及纖維軟骨關節盤（articular disc） 之間。關節盤將 radio-ulnar 關節與腕關節分開。

三角形的 articular disc（關節盤） 由其 apex 附著於 ulna 上 styloid process 和頭部關節面之間的粗糙凹陷處，base 則附著於 radius 上 ulnar notch 和腕骨關節面之間的 angular margin。

遠端 radio-ulnar 關節允許 radius 的遠端在 ulna 上向前內側移動。

Interosseous Membrane（骨間膜）

Interosseous membrane（骨間膜） 是一層薄的纖維膜，連接 radius 和 ulna 分別的內側和外側邊界。膜內的膠原蛋白纖維主要從 radius 斜向下方至 ulna。

骨間膜有一個遊離的上緣，位於 radial tuberosity 正下方；在其遠端三分之一處有一個小圓形孔隙。血管在 upper margin 上方在 anterior 和 posterior compartments 之間通行，並穿過下方的孔隙。

骨間膜連接 radius 和 ulna，且不妨礙 pronation 和 supination，並為前臂前側和後側 compartments 的肌肉提供附著處。膜內纖維的排列方向也與其將力量從 radius 轉移至 ulna、最終從手轉移至肱骨的功能一致。

Pronation 與 Supination（旋前與旋後）

手的 pronation 和 supination 完全發生在前臂，涉及 radius 在肘部的旋轉和 radius 遠端在 ulna 上的移動。

在肘部，radial head 的上關節面在 capitulum 上旋轉，同時頭部側面的關節面在 ulna 的 radial notch 及關節囊的相鄰區域和 anular ligament of the radius 上滑動。在遠端 radio-ulnar 關節，radius 的 ulnar notch 在 ulna 頭部的凸面上向前滑動。

在這些運動中，骨骼由以下結構固定在一起：

  • 近端 radio-ulnar 關節的 anular ligament of the radius
  • 沿 radius 和 ulna 全長的 interosseous membrane
  • 遠端 radio-ulnar 關節的 articular disc

因為手主要與 radius 關節，radius 遠端在 ulna 上向內側的移位使手從掌心向前（supinated）位置移動到掌心向後（pronated）位置。

參與 Pronation 與 Supination 的肌肉

Supinator（旋後肌）：位於前臂後側 compartment，源於 ulna 的 supinator crest 和肱骨的 lateral epicondyle，以及與肘關節相關的韌帶。Supinator 肌肉繞過 radius 上三分之一的后侧面和外侧面，附著於骨幹，位置在 oblique line 上方。當手處於 pronated 位置時，biceps brachii 和 supinator 的肌腱都繞過 radius 近端。當它們收縮時，會從骨骼上展開，產生手的 supination。

Pronator teres 與 Pronator quadratus：Pronation 來自 pronator teres 和 pronator quadratus 肌肉的作用。這兩塊肌肉都位於前臂前側 compartment：

  • Pronator teres：從肱骨的 medial epicondyle 延伸至 radius 中段附近的 lateral surface
  • Pronator quadratus：在 radius 和 ulna 遠端的前表面之間延伸

當這些肌肉收縮時，它們拉動 radius 遠端越過 ulna，產生手的 pronation。

Anconeus：除了肘關節的鉸鏈式屈伸外，還發生 ulna 遠端的一些外展，維持手的掌心在 pronation 期間圍繞中心軸的位置。參與此運動的肌肉是 anconeus muscle，這是前臂後側 compartment 中的一塊三角形肌肉，從 lateral epicondyle 延伸至 ulna 近端的外側 surface。

前臂前側 Compartment（Anterior Compartment）的肌肉

前臂前側（屈肌）compartment 的肌肉分為三層：淺層（superficial）、中層（intermediate） 和 深層（deep）。這些肌肉通常與以下功能相關：

  • 腕關節的運動
  • 手指（包括拇指）的屈曲
  • Pronation

前臂前側 compartment 的所有肌肉都由 median nerve 神經支配，但 flexor carpi ulnaris 和 flexor digitorum profundus 的內側半由 ulnar nerve 神經支配。

淺層肌肉（Superficial Layer）

淺層的四塊肌肉——flexor carpi ulnaris、palmaris longus、flexor carpi radialis 和 pronator teres——都源自肱骨的 medial epicondyle，除 pronator teres 外，都從前臂延伸至手部。

Flexor Carpi Ulnaris（尺側腕屈肌）

Flexor carpi ulnaris 是淺層屈肌中最內側的肌肉，除了源自肱骨的 medial epicondyle 外，還從 olecranon 和 ulna 的後 border 有很長的線性起始。

Ulnar nerve 通過 flexor carpi ulnaris 的 humeral head 和 ulnar head 之間的三角形間隙進入前臂前側 compartment。肌肉纖維匯聚成一條肌腱，向遠端延伸並附著於手腕的 pisiform bone（豌豆骨）。從此處，力透過 pisohamate ligament 和 pisometacarpal ligament 傳遞至手腕的 hamate bone（鉤骨） 和 metacarpal V（第五掌骨） 的底部。

Flexor carpi ulnaris 是手腕有力的屈肌和內收肌，由 ulnar nerve 神經支配。

Palmaris Longus（掌長肌）

Palmaris longus 約存在於 85% 的人群中，介於 flexor carpi ulnaris 和 flexor carpi radialis 之間。這是一塊紡錘形肌肉，具有一條長肌腱，伸入手部並附著於 flexor retinaculum（屈肌支持帶） 和深層筋膜的厚層——palmar aponeurosis（掌腱膜），位於手掌和手指皮膚的下方並與之附著。

除了作為手腕關節的輔助屈肌外，palmaris longus 還在握持時抵抗手掌皮膚的剪切力。

Flexor Carpi Radialis（橈側腕屈肌）

Flexor carpi radialis 位於 palmaris longus 的外側，在前臂遠端有一條大而明顯的肌腱。與形成前臂遠端內側邊緣的 flexor carpi ulnaris 肌腱不同，flexor carpi radialis 的肌腱位於正中線的外側。在此位置，肌腱容易觸診，成為尋找位於其外側的 radial artery（橈動脈） 脈搏的重要標誌。

Flexor carpi radialis 的肌腱穿過手腕外側由骨和筋膜形成的 compartment，附著於 metacarpals II 和 III 底部的 anterior surfaces。Flexor carpi radialis 是手腕有力的屈肌，也能使手腕外展。

Pronator Teres（旋前圓肌）

Pronator teres 源自肱骨的 medial epicondyle 和 supraepicondylar ridge，以及 ulna coronoid process 內側邊緣的一小線性區域。Median nerve 常通過此肌肉的 humeral head 和 ulnar head 之間離開 cubital fossa。Pronator teres 跨越前臂，附著於 radius 中段附近的 lateral surface 的橢圓形粗糙區。

Pronator teres 形成 cubital fossa（肘窩） 的內側邊界，在 pronation 期間使 radius 繞 ulna 旋轉。

肌肉 起始 附著 神經支配 功能
Flexor carpi ulnaris 肱骨頭—肱骨 medial epicondyle；尺骨頭—olecranon 和 ulna 後 border Pisiform bone，經 pisohamate 和 pisometacarpal ligaments 至 hamate 和 metacarpal V 底部 Ulnar nerve (C7, C8, T1) 屈曲和內收腕關節
Palmaris longus 肱骨 medial epicondyle 手掌的 palmar aponeurosis Median nerve (C7, C8) 屈腕；抵抗握持時的剪切力
Flexor carpi radialis 肱骨 medial epicondyle Metacarpals II 和 III 底部 Median nerve (C6, C7) 屈曲和外展腕關節
Pronator teres 肱骨頭—medial epicondyle 和相鄰 supra-epicondylar ridge；尺骨頭—coronoid process 內側 Radius 中段外側面的粗糙區 Median nerve (C6, C7) Pronation

中層肌肉（Intermediate Layer）

Flexor Digitorum Superficialis（淺指屈肌）

前臂前側 compartment 中層的肌肉是 flexor digitorum superficialis。這塊大肌肉有兩個 head：

  • Humero-ulnar head：主要源自肱骨的 medial epicondyle 和 ulna coronoid process 相鄰的內側邊緣
  • Radial head：源自 radius 的 anterior oblique line

Median nerve 和 ulnar artery 從兩個 heads 之間深層通過 flexor digitorum superficialis。

在遠端前臂，flexor digitorum superficialis 形成四條肌腱，穿過手腕的 carpal tunnel 進入四根手指。環指和中指的肌腱位於食指和小指肌腱的淺層。

在前臂、carpal tunnel 和四根手指的近端區域，flexor digitorum superficialis 的肌腱位於 flexor digitorum profundus 肌腱的前方。

在每根手指近端指骨底部附近，flexor digitorum superficialis 的肌腱分叉成兩部分，繞過 flexor digitorum profundus 肌腱的兩側，最終附著於**中指骨（middle phalanx）**的邊緣。

Flexor digitorum superficialis 屈曲每根手指的掌指關節（metacarpophalangeal joint）和近端指間關節（proximal interphalangeal joint）；也能屈曲腕關節。

肌肉 起始 附著 神經支配 功能
Flexor digitorum superficialis Humero-ulnar head—肱骨 medial epicondyle 和 coronoid process 相鄰邊緣；Radial head—radius oblique line 四條肌腱，附著於食指、中指、環指和小指中指骨的掌側面 Median nerve (C8, T1) 屈曲食指、中指、環指和小指的近端指間關節；也能屈曲相同手指的掌指關節和腕關節

Gray’s Anatomy — Upper Limb

前臂（前腔室）深層肌肉

Flexor Digitorum Profundus（指深屈肌）

前臂前腔室有三塊深層肌肉：flexor digitorum profundus、flexor pollicis longus、和 pronator quadratus（圖 7.85）。

Flexor digitorum profundus 肌肉起點為尺骨的前面及內側面，以及骨間膜前面的內側半部（圖 7.85）。它發出四條肌腱，經過腕隧道進入四個內側手指。在大部分行程中，這些肌腱都位於 flexor digitorum superficialis 肌肉肌腱的深層。

在每根手指的proximal phalanx（近節指骨）的對側，每條 flexor digitorum profundus 的肌腱穿過覆蓋其上的 flexor digitorum superficialis 肌腱形成的裂隙，然後遠行，附著於遠節指骨底部的前面。

在手掌中，**lumbrical muscles（小魚際肌）**起點為 flexor digitorum profundus 肌腱的兩側（見圖 7.104）。

Flexor digitorum profundus 的內側半和外側半的神經支配如下：

  • 外側半（與食指和中指相關）由正中神經的前骨間分支（anterior interosseous nerve）支配。
  • 內側半（與無名指和小指相關）由尺神經支配。

Flexor digitorum profundus 可屈曲四指 的metacarpophalangeal joints（掌指關節）、proximal interphalangeal joints（近端指間關節）和distal interphalangeal joints（遠端指間關節）。由於肌腱跨越腕關節，它也能屈曲腕關節（表 7.12）。

臨床重點：**Lateral half（外側半）**由正中神經（anterior interosseous nerve）支配，**medial half（內側半）**由尺神經支配。這解釋了為何正中神經損傷時食指和中指屈曲力量減弱，而尺神經損傷時無名指和小指受影響。

Flexor Pollicis Longus（拇指長屈肌）

Flexor pollicis longus 肌肉起點為橈骨前面及骨間膜前面的橈側半（圖 7.85）。它是一塊強大的肌肉，形成一條粗大的肌腱，經過腕隧道，位於 flexor digitorum superficialis 和 flexor digitorum profundus 肌肉肌腱的外側，進入拇指並附著於遠節指骨底部。

Flexor pollicis longus 可屈曲拇指，由正中神經的前骨間分支支配（表 7.12）。

Pronator Quadratus（旋前方肌）

Pronator quadratus 肌肉是遠端前臂中一塊扁平的方形肌肉（圖 7.85）。它起點為尺骨下端前面的線性脊，向外側橫行，附著於橈骨前面的扁平表面。它位於 flexor digitorum profundus 和 flexor pollicis longus 肌肉肌腱的深層，並被這些肌腱跨越。

Pronator quadratus 肌肉在旋前時將橈骨遠端向前拉過尺骨，由正中神經的前骨間分支支配（表 7.12）。

表 7.12 — 前臂前腔室深層肌肉

肌肉 起點 附著點 神經支配 功能
Flexor digitorum profundus 尺骨前面及內側面、骨間膜內側半 四條肌腱附著於食指、中指、無名指、小指的遠節指骨底部的掌側表面 外側半：正中神經（anterior interosseous nerve）；內側半：尺神經（C8, T1） 屈曲食指、中指、無名指、小指的遠端指間關節；也能屈曲同指的掌指關節及腕關節
Flexor pollicis longus 橈骨前面、骨間膜橈側半 拇指遠節指骨底的掌側表面 正中神經（前骨間分支）（C7, C8） 屈曲拇指的指間關節；也能屈曲拇指的掌指關節
Pronator quadratus 尺骨遠端前面的線性脊 橈骨遠端前面 正中神經（前骨間分支）（C7, C8） 旋前

前臂前腔室的動脈與靜脈

前臂最大的動脈位於前腔室，向遠端延伸供應手部，並發出分支供應後腔室（圖 7.86）。

**Brachial artery（肱動脈）從臂部經過肘窩（cubital fossa）**進入前臂。在肘窩尖部，它分為兩條主要分支：**radial artery（橈動脈）**和 ulnar artery（尺動脈）。

Radial Artery（橈動脈）

Radial artery 起點約在橈骨頸處由 brachial artery 分出，沿前臂外側行走（圖 7.86）：

  • 在前臂近側半，它位於 brachioradialis 肌肉的深層。
  • 在前臂中三分之一處，其外側與橈神經的淺支相鄰。
  • 在遠端前臂，位於 brachioradialis 肌腱的內側，只被深筋膜、淺筋膜和皮膚覆蓋。

在遠端前臂，radial artery 緊鄰 flexor carpi radialis 粗大肌腱的外側，直接位於 pronator quadratus 肌肉和橈骨遠端的前面（圖 7.86）。在遠端前臂，可利用 flexor carpi radialis 肌肉作為標誌來定位 radial artery。輕輕觸摸 radial artery 即可感受到橈動脈搏動。

Radial artery 離開前臂，繞過腕關節外側，穿過第一和第二掌骨底之間進入手的後外側（圖 7.86）。Radial artery 在手上的分支通常是拇指和食指橈側的主要血液供應。

Radial artery 在前臂的分支包括：

  • Radial recurrent artery（橈側返動脈）：參與肘關節周圍的吻合血管網，並為 pronator teres 提供營養。
  • Palmar carpal branch（掌側腕支）：參與供應腕骨和關節的吻合血管網。
  • Superficial palmar branch（淺掌支）：經過或淺行穿過魚際肌進入手部，與 ulnar artery 形成的淺掌弓吻合（圖 7.86）。

臨床重點：橈動脈位置表淺，在遠端前臂沿 flexor carpi radialis 肌腱內側走行，臨床上可在此處觸及橈動脈搏動（把脈）。這也是臨床上常選用的抽血和置管部位。

Ulnar Artery（尺動脈）

Ulnar artery 比 radial artery 粗大，沿前臂內側下行（圖 7.86）。它從肘窩穿過 pronator teres 肌肉深層離開，然後在前臂的 flexor carpi ulnaris 和 flexor digitorum profundus 肌肉之間的筋膜平面中穿行。

在遠端前臂，ulnar artery 通常藏在 flexor carpi ulnaris 肌腱的前外側唇下方，因此不易觸及。

在遠端前臂，**ulnar nerve（尺神經）**緊鄰 ulnar artery 的內側。

Ulnar artery 離開前臂，經過豌豆骨的外側和腕屈肌支持帶的淺層入手，在手掌形成弓形（圖 7.86）。它通常是小指側三個半手指的主要血液供應。

Ulnar artery 在前臂的分支包括：

  • Ulnar recurrent artery（尺側返動脈）：有前支和後支，參與肘關節周圍的吻合血管網。
  • 多條肌支：供應周圍肌肉。
  • Common interosseous artery（骨間總動脈）：分為前骨間動脈和後骨間動脈（圖 7.86）。
  • 兩條小的腕支（dorsal carpal branch 和 palmar carpal branch）：供應腕關節。

**Posterior interosseous artery（後骨間動脈）**從骨間膜近側緣的背側穿過，進入前臂後腔室。

Anterior interosseous artery（前骨間動脈）沿骨間膜前面向遠端行走，供應前臂深腔室肌肉和橈骨、尺骨。它有許多分支穿過骨間膜，供應後腔室的深層肌肉；它也有一小分支參與腕骨和關節周圍的血管網。在遠端前臂穿過骨間膜時，前骨間動脈終止並與後骨間動脈會合。

靜脈

前臂前腔室的深靜脈通常伴行於同名动脉，最終流入位於肘窩的肱靜脈。

臨床重點：橈動脈或尺動脈的橫斷傷在成人患者中並不少見，因為這些血管相對淺表。受傷的典型方式是手被迫穿過平板玻璃窗。幸運的是，手的双重血供通常使外科醫生能夠結紮尺動脈或橈動脈而不會造成嚴重後果。

前臂前腔室的神經

前臂前腔室的神經有：正中神經、尺神經和橈神經的淺支（圖 7.87）。

Median Nerve（正中神經）

正中神經支配前臂前腔室的肌肉，除了 flexor carpi ulnaris 和 flexor digitorum profundus 的內側部分（無名指和小指）。它從肘窩穿過 pronator teres 肌肉的兩個頭之間離開，然後穿過 flexor digitorum superficialis 肌肉的肱尺頭和橈側頭之間（圖 7.87）。

正中神經沿前臂遠端在 flexor digitorum superficialis 肌肉深層的筋膜中直線下行。就在腕關節近側，它繞過肌肉的外側，變得較淺表，位於 palmaris longus 和 flexor carpi radialis 肌肉的肌腱之間。它離開前臂並經過腕隧道（屈肌支持帶深層）入手。

大多數淺層和中層肌肉的神經分支在肘關節遠側由神經的內側發出。

  • 正中神經在前臂最大的分支是前骨間神經，起點在 pronator teres 的兩個頭之間，沿前臂與前骨間動脈一起向遠端行走，支配深層肌肉（flexor pollicis longus、flexor digitorum profundus 的外側半和 pronator quadratus），終於遠端前臂和腕關節的關節支。
  • 一個小的掌支起點在遠端前臂，就在屈肌支持帶的近側（圖 7.87），淺行入手，支配手基底部和掌心中央的皮膚。這個掌支在腕隧道症候群中不受影響，因為它經過腕屈肌支持帶的淺層入手。

臨床重點：**掌支（Palmar branch）**在腕隧道症候群中不受影響，因為它不穿過腕隧道，而是從屈肌支持帶淺層經過。這也是腕隧道症候群主要影響魚際肌（thenar muscles）和手指感覺，而手部掌心的感覺通常保留的原因。

Ulnar Nerve（尺神經）

尺神經穿過前臂入手，其大多數主要分支在手部。在前臂，尺神經只支配 flexor carpi ulnaris 肌肉和 flexor digitorum profundus 的內側部分（無名指和小指）（圖 7.87）。

尺神經穿過前臂前腔室時，從肱骨內上髁後方繞過，穿過 flexor carpi ulnaris 肌肉的肱骨頭和尺骨頭之間（圖 7.87）。它沿前臂內側在 flexor carpi ulnaris 和 flexor digitorum profundus 肌肉之間的平面下行，在腕關節近側，它位於 flexor carpi ulnaris 肌腱的外側唇下方。

在前臂遠端三分之二，尺神經位於 ulnar artery 的內側，兩者都經過豌豆骨的外側和屈肌支持帶的淺層入手（圖 7.87）。

尺神經在前臂發出的分支：

  • 肌支：支配 flexor carpi ulnaris 和 flexor digitorum profundus 的內側半，在尺神經進入前臂後不久發出。
  • 兩條小的皮支：掌支起源於前臂中段，淺行入手，支配手掌內側的皮膚；較大的背支起源於前臂遠端，向後穿過 flexor carpi ulnaris 肌腱深層，支配手背內側和大部分小指側一個半手指背面的皮膚。

Radial Nerve（橈神經）

橈神經在肘窩外側緣的 brachioradialis 肌肉邊緣下方分為深支和淺支（圖 7.87）：

  • 深支主要是運動神經，穿過 supinator 肌肉的兩個頭之間進入並支配前臂後腔室的肌肉。
  • 橈神經的淺支是感覺神經。它沿前臂前外側下行，深層位於 brachioradialis 肌肉下方，並與 radial artery 相鄰。在前臂約三分之二處，橈神經的淺支繞過前臂橈側和背側，深層位於 brachioradialis 肌腱下方，然後進入手部，支配手背橈側的皮膚。

臨床重點：尺神經在前臂只支配兩塊肌肉：flexor carpi ulnaris 和 flexor digitorum profundus 的內側半（無名指和小指）。尺神經損傷會導致手指內收和外展無力（lumbricals 和 interossei 麻痺），以及手掌內側和手背的感覺障礙。

前臂後腔室

肌肉

前臂後腔室的肌肉分為兩層：淺層和深層。這些肌肉與以下運動相關：

  • 腕關節的運動
  • 手指和拇指的伸展
  • 旋後（supination）

前臂後腔室的所有肌肉都由橈神經支配。

淺層

淺層有七塊肌肉：brachioradialis、extensor carpi radialis longus、extensor carpi radialis brevis、extensor digitorum、extensor digiti minimi、extensor carpi ulnaris 和 anconeus（圖 7.88）。它們都有一個共同的起點：肱骨的上髁嵴（supraepicondylar ridge）和外上髁（lateral epicondyle）。除了 brachioradialis 和 anconeus 外，其餘都延伸出肌腱入手。

Brachioradialis（肱橈肌）

Brachioradialis 肌肉起點為肱骨上髁嵴的近側部分，穿過前臂附著於橈骨遠端的外側，正好在**橈骨莖突（radial styloid process）**的近側（圖 7.88）。

在解剖學姿勢中，brachioradialis 是前臂前外側面上的肌肉塊的一部分，形成肘窩的外側界。

因為 brachioradialis 位於肘關節的前面，所以它是這個關節的輔助屈肌，即使它位於前臂的後腔室。它的作用在前臂中等程度的旋前位時最有效，當它對抗阻力時會形成明顯的隆起。

橈神經從臂部後腔室在 brachioradialis 深層的遠端臂部發出，支配 brachioradialis。在肘窩外側，brachioradialis 位於橈神經及其分為深淺支的上方。在更遠端，brachioradialis 位於橈骨的上方。

Extensor Carpi Radialis Longus（橈側腕長伸肌）

起點：肱骨外上髁（上髁嵴的遠端部分）。止點：第二掌骨底背面。功能：伸腕並輕度外展。神經支配：橈神經（C6, C7）。

Extensor Carpi Radialis Brevis（橈側腕短伸肌）

起點：肱骨外上髁。止點：第三掌骨底背面。功能：伸腕。神經支配：橈神經深支（C7, C8）。

Extensor Digitorum（指伸肌）

起點：肱骨外上髁。止點：通過四條肌腱附著於食指、中指、無名指和小指的遠節指骨和中節指骨背面。功能：伸四指的所有指間關節及掌指關節。神經支配：橈神經深支。

Extensor Digiti Minimi（小指伸肌）

起點：肱骨外上髁（與 extensor digitorum 共腱）。止點：小指指骨背面。功能：單獨伸小指。神經支配：橈神經深支。

Extensor Carpi Ulnaris（尺側腕伸肌）

起點：肱骨外上髁及尺骨背面。止點：第五掌骨底。功能：伸腕並內收。神經支配：橈神經深支。

Anconeus（肘肌）

起點：肱骨外上髁。止點：尺骨背面近端。功能：協助伸肘。神經支配：桡神經（C7, C8）。

臨床重點：前臂後腔室的所有肌肉都由橈神經支配。橈神經損傷（特別是深支）在前臂後腔室會導致**腕下垂（wrist drop）**和手指伸展無力，因為伸腕和伸指的肌肉全部癱瘓。

Regional Anatomy — Posterior Compartment of the Forearm

Superficial Layer of Muscles

Extensor Carpi Radialis Longus

The extensor carpi radialis longus muscle originates from the distal part of the supraepicondylar ridge and the lateral epicondyle of the humerus; its tendon inserts on the dorsal surface of the base of metacarpal II (Fig. 7.88). In proximal regions, it is deep to the brachioradialis muscle.

The extensor carpi radialis longus extends and abducts the wrist, and is innervated by the radial nerve before the nerve divides into superficial and deep branches.

臨床重點：當 radial nerve 受損時，腕關節的伸直及外展功能會受到影響，導致「垂腕」（wrist drop）現象。

Extensor Carpi Radialis Brevis

The extensor carpi radialis brevis muscle originates from the lateral epicondyle of the humerus, and the tendon inserts onto adjacent dorsal surfaces of the bases of metacarpals II and III (Fig. 7.88). Along much of its course, the extensor carpi radialis brevis lies deep to the extensor carpi radialis longus.

The extensor carpi radialis brevis extends and abducts the wrist, and is innervated by the deep branch of the radial nerve before the nerve passes between the two heads of the supinator muscle.

Extensor Digitorum

The extensor digitorum muscle is the major extensor of the four fingers (index, middle, ring, and little fingers). It originates from the lateral epicondyle of the humerus and forms four tendons, each of which passes into a finger (Fig. 7.88).

On the dorsal surface of the hand, adjacent tendons of the extensor digitorum are interconnected. In the fingers, each tendon inserts, via a triangular-shaped connective tissue aponeurosis (the extensor hood), into the base of the dorsal surfaces of the middle and distal phalanges.

The extensor digitorum is innervated by the posterior interosseous nerve, which is the continuation of the deep branch of the radial nerve after it emerges from the supinator muscle.

Extensor Digiti Minimi

The extensor digiti minimi muscle is an accessory extensor of the little finger and is medial to the extensor digitorum in the forearm (Fig. 7.88). It originates from the lateral epicondyle of the humerus and inserts, together with the tendon of the extensor digitorum, into the extensor hood of the little finger.

The extensor digiti minimi is innervated by the posterior interosseous nerve.

Extensor Carpi Ulnaris

The extensor carpi ulnaris muscle is medial to the extensor digiti minimi (Fig. 7.88). It originates from the lateral epicondyle, and its tendon inserts into the medial side of the base of metacarpal V.

The extensor carpi ulnaris extends and adducts the wrist, and is innervated by the posterior interosseous nerve.

Anconeus

The anconeus muscle is the most medial of the superficial extensors and has a triangular shape. It originates from the lateral epicondyle of the humerus and has a broad insertion into the posterolateral surface of the olecranon and related posterior surface of the ulna (see Fig. 7.82).

The anconeus abducts the ulna during pronation to maintain the center of the palm over the same point when the hand is flipped. It is also considered to be an accessory extensor of the elbow joint.

The anconeus is innervated by the branch of the radial nerve that innervates the medial head of the triceps brachii muscle.

Table 7.13 — Superficial Layer of Muscles in the Posterior Compartment of the Forearm

Muscle Origin Insertion Innervation Function

Extensor carpi radialis longus Distal part of lateral supraepicondylar ridge of humerus and adjacent intermuscular septum Dorsal surface of base of metacarpal II Radial nerve (C6, C7) before division into superficial and deep branches Extends and abducts the wrist
Extensor carpi radialis brevis Lateral epicondyle of humerus and adjacent intermuscular septum Dorsal surface of base of metacarpals II and III Deep branch of radial nerve (C7, C8) before penetrating supinator muscle Extends and abducts the wrist
Extensor digitorum Lateral epicondyle of humerus and adjacent intermuscular septum and deep fascia Four tendons, which insert via extensor hoods into the dorsal aspects of the bases of the middle and distal phalanges of the index, middle, ring, and little fingers Posterior interosseous nerve (C7, C8) Extends the index, middle, ring, and little fingers; can also extend the wrist
Extensor digiti minimi Lateral epicondyle of humerus and adjacent intermuscular septum Extensor hood of the little finger Posterior interosseous nerve (C7, C8) Extends the little finger together with extensor digitorum
Extensor carpi ulnaris Lateral epicondyle of humerus and posterior border of ulna Tubercle on the base of the medial side of metacarpal V Posterior interosseous nerve (C7, C8) Extends and adducts the wrist
Anconeus Lateral epicondyle of humerus Olecranon and proximal posterior surface of ulna Radial nerve (C6, C7, C8) (via branch to medial head of triceps brachii) Abduction of the ulna in pronation; accessory extensor of the elbow joint

Deep Layer of Muscles

The deep layer of the posterior compartment of the forearm consists of five muscles: supinator, abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, extensor pollicis longus, and extensor indicis (Fig. 7.89).

Except for the supinator muscle, all these deep layer muscles originate from the posterior surfaces of the radius, ulna, and interosseous membrane and pass into the thumb and fingers.

  • Three of these muscles—the abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, and extensor pollicis longus—emerge from between the extensor digitorum and the extensor carpi radialis brevis tendons of the superficial layer and pass into the thumb.
  • Two of the three “outcropping” muscles (the abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis) form a distinct muscular bulge in the distal posterolateral surface of the forearm.

All muscles of the deep layer are innervated by the posterior interosseous nerve, the continuation of the deep branch of the radial nerve.

Supinator

The supinator muscle has two heads of origin, which insert together on the proximal aspect of the radius (Fig. 7.89):

  • The superficial (humeral) head originates mainly from the lateral epicondyle of the humerus and the related anular ligament and the radial collateral ligament of the elbow joint.
  • The deep (ulnar) head originates mainly from the supinator crest on the posterolateral surface of the ulna.

From their sites of origin, the two heads wrap around the posterior and lateral aspect of the head, neck, and proximal shaft of the radius to insert on the lateral surface of the radius superior to the anterior oblique line and to the insertion of the pronator teres muscle.

The supinator muscle supinates the forearm and hand.

The deep branch of the radial nerve innervates the supinator muscle and passes to the posterior compartment of the forearm by passing between the two heads of this muscle.

臨床重點：Supinator muscle 的兩個頭之間是 radial nerve 的 deep branch（後成為 posterior interosseous nerve）的通道，手術時需特別注意避免損傷。

Abductor Pollicis Longus

The abductor pollicis longus muscle originates from the proximal posterior surfaces of the radius and the ulna and from the related interosseous membrane (Fig. 7.89). In the distal forearm, it emerges between the extensor digitorum and extensor carpi radialis brevis muscles to form a tendon that passes into the thumb and inserts on the lateral side of the base of metacarpal I. The tendon contributes to the lateral border of the anatomical snuffbox at the wrist.

The major function of the abductor pollicis longus is to abduct the thumb at the joint between the metacarpal I and trapezium bones.

Extensor Pollicis Brevis

The extensor pollicis brevis muscle arises distal to the origin of the abductor pollicis longus from the posterior surface of the radius and interosseous membrane (Fig. 7.89). Together with the abductor pollicis longus, it emerges between the extensor digitorum and extensor carpi radialis brevis muscles to form a bulge on the posterolateral surface of the distal forearm. The tendon of the extensor pollicis brevis passes into the thumb and inserts on the dorsal surface of the base of the proximal phalanx.

At the wrist, the tendon contributes to the lateral border of the anatomical snuffbox.

The extensor pollicis brevis extends the metacarpophalangeal and carpometacarpal joints of the thumb.

Extensor Pollicis Longus

The extensor pollicis longus muscle originates from the posterior surface of the ulna and adjacent interosseous membrane and inserts via a long tendon into the dorsal surface of the distal phalanx of the thumb (Fig. 7.89).

Like the abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis, the tendon of this muscle emerges between the extensor digitorum and the extensor carpi radialis brevis muscles. However, it is held away from the other two deep muscles of the thumb by passing medially around the dorsal tubercle on the distal end of the radius. The tendon forms the medial margin of the anatomical snuffbox at the wrist.

The extensor pollicis longus extends all joints of the thumb.

臨床重點：Anatomical snuffbox 是臨床上重要的解剖區域，其邊界由三條肌腱構成：橈側為 abductor pollicis longus 及 extensor pollicis brevis 的肌腱，尺側為 extensor pollicis longus 的肌腱。Scaphoid 骨折時，此區域常有壓痛。

Extensor Indicis

The extensor indicis muscle is an accessory extensor of the index finger. It originates distal to the extensor pollicis longus from the posterior surface of the ulna and adjacent interosseous membrane (Fig. 7.89). The tendon passes into the hand and inserts into the extensor hood of the index finger with the tendon of the extensor digitorum.

Abductor pollicis longus Posterior surfaces of ulna and radius (distal to the attachments of supinator and anconeus), and intervening interosseous membrane Lateral side of base of metacarpal I Posterior interosseous nerve (C7, C8) Abducts carpometacarpal joint of thumb; accessory extensor of the thumb

Arteries and Veins

The blood supply to the posterior compartment of the forearm occurs predominantly through branches of the radial, posterior interosseous, and anterior interosseous arteries (Fig. 7.90).

Posterior Interosseous Artery

The posterior interosseous artery originates in the anterior compartment from the common interosseous branch of the ulnar artery and passes posteriorly over the proximal margin of the interosseous membrane and into the posterior compartment of the forearm. It contributes a branch, the recurrent interosseous artery, to the vascular network around the elbow joint and then passes between the supinator and abductor pollicis longus muscles to supply the superficial extensors. After receiving the terminal end of the anterior interosseous artery, the posterior interosseous artery terminates by joining the dorsal carpal arch of the wrist.

Anterior Interosseous Artery

The anterior interosseous artery, also a branch of the common interosseous branch of the ulnar artery, is situated in the anterior compartment of the forearm on the interosseous membrane. It has numerous perforating branches, which pass directly through the interosseous membrane to supply deep muscles of the posterior compartment. The terminal end of the anterior interosseous artery passes posteriorly through an aperture in the interosseous membrane in distal regions of the forearm to join the posterior interosseous artery.

Radial Artery

The radial artery has muscular branches, which contribute to the supply of the extensor muscles on the radial side of the forearm.

Veins

Deep veins of the posterior compartment generally accompany the arteries. They ultimately drain into brachial veins associated with the brachial artery in the cubital fossa.

Nerves

Radial Nerve

The nerve of the posterior compartment of the forearm is the radial nerve (Fig. 7.90). Most of the muscles are innervated by the deep branch, which originates from the radial nerve in the lateral wall of the cubital fossa deep to the brachioradialis muscle and becomes the posterior interosseous nerve after emerging from between the two heads of the supinator muscle in the posterior compartment of the forearm.

In the lateral wall of the cubital fossa, and before dividing into superficial and deep branches, the radial nerve innervates the brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus muscles.

The deep branch innervates the extensor carpi radialis brevis, then passes between the two heads of the supinator muscle and follows the plane of separation between the two heads dorsally and laterally around the proximal shaft of the radius to the posterior aspect of the forearm. It supplies the supinator muscle and then emerges, as the posterior interosseous nerve, from the muscle to lie between the superficial and deep layers of muscles.

The posterior interosseous nerve supplies the remaining muscles in the posterior compartment and terminates as articular branches, which pass deep to the extensor pollicis longus muscle to reach the wrist.

Hand

The hand (Fig. 7.91) is the region of the upper limb distal to the wrist joint. It is subdivided into three parts:

  • the wrist (carpus)
  • the metacarpus
  • the digits (five fingers including the thumb)

The five digits consist of the laterally positioned thumb and, medial to the thumb, the four fingers—the index, middle, ring, and little fingers.

In the normal resting position, the fingers form a flexed arcade, with the little finger flexed most and the index finger flexed least. In the anatomical position, the fingers are extended.

The hand has an anterior surface (palm) and a dorsal surface (dorsum of hand).

Abduction and adduction of the fingers are defined with respect to the long axis of the middle finger (Fig. 7.91). In the anatomical position, the long axis of the thumb is rotated 90° to the rest of the digits so that the pad of the thumb points medially; consequently, movements of the thumb are defined at right angles to the movements of the other digits of the hand.

The hand is a mechanical and sensory tool. Many of the features of the upper limb are designed to facilitate positioning the hand in space.

Bones

There are three groups of bones in the hand:

  • The eight carpal bones are the bones of the wrist.
  • The five metacarpals (I to V) are the bones of the metacarpus.
  • The phalanges are the bones of the digits—the thumb has only two; the rest of the digits have three (Fig. 7.92).

The carpal bones and metacarpals of the index, middle, ring, and little fingers (metacarpals II to V) tend to function as a unit and form much of the bony framework of the palm. The metacarpal of the thumb functions independently and has increased flexibility at the carpometacarpal joint to provide opposition of the thumb to the fingers.

Carpal Bones

The small carpal bones of the wrist are arranged in two rows, a proximal and a distal row, each consisting of four bones (Fig. 7.92).

Proximal Row

From lateral to medial and when viewed from anteriorly, the proximal row of bones consists of:

  • the boat-shaped scaphoid
  • the lunate, which has a crescent shape
  • the three-sided triquetrum bone
  • the pea-shaped pisiform (Fig. 7.92)

The pisiform is a sesamoid bone in the tendon of the flexor carpi ulnaris and articulates with the anterior surface of the triquetrum.

The scaphoid has a prominent tubercle on its lateral palmar surface that is directed anteriorly.

臨床重點：Scaphoid 是腕骨中最常骨折的骨頭，常因跌倒時手部外展撐地造成。因血液供應特殊，骨折後有缺血性壞死的風險。臨床上觸摸 scaphoid tubercle 有助於定位此骨頭。

Distal Row

From lateral to medial and when viewed from anteriorly, the distal row of carpal bones consists of:

  • the irregular four-sided trapezium bone
  • the four-sided trapezoid
  • the capitate, which has a head
  • the hamate, which has a hook (Fig. 7.92)

The trapezium articulates with the metacarpal bone of the thumb and has a distinct tubercle on its palmar surface that projects anteriorly.

The largest of the carpal bones, the capitate, articulates with the base of metacarpal III.

The hamate, which is positioned just lateral and distal to the pisiform, has a prominent hook (hook of hamate) on its palmar surface that projects anteriorly.

臨床重點：Hook of hamate 骨折可因球類運動（如高爾夫球、棒球）中使用球桿或球棒時，手柄直接撞擊而發生。臨床上可透過觸摸小鱼际隆起（hypothenar eminence）遠端來檢查。

Articular Surfaces

The carpal bones have numerous articular surfaces (Fig. 7.92). All of them articulate with each other, and the carpal bones in the distal row articulate with the metacarpals of the digits. With the exception of the metacarpal of the thumb, all movements of the metacarpal bones on the carpal bones are limited.

The expansive proximal surfaces of the scaphoid and lunate articulate with the radius to form the wrist joint.

Carpal Arch

The carpal bones do not lie in a flat plane; rather, they form an arch, whose base is directed anteriorly (Fig. 7.92). The lateral side of this base is formed by the tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium. The medial side is formed by the pisiform and the hook of the hamate.

The flexor retinaculum attaches to, and spans the distance between, the medial and lateral sides of the base to form the anterior wall of the so-called carpal tunnel. The sides and roof of the carpal tunnel are formed by the arch of the carpal bones.

臨床重點：Carpal tunnel syndrome 是由 flexor retinaculum 對 median nerve 造成的壓迫所引起，常見於重複性手部動作的職業病。症狀包括拇指、食指、中指及無名指橈側的麻木與刺痛。

Metacarpals

Each of the five metacarpals is related to one digit:

  • Metacarpal I is related to the thumb.
  • Metacarpals II to V are related to the index, middle, ring, and little fingers, respectively (Fig. 7.92).

Each metacarpal consists of a base, a shaft (body), and distally, a head.

All of the bases of the metacarpals articulate with the carpal bones; in addition, the bases of the metacarpal bones of the fingers articulate with each other.

All of the heads of the metacarpals articulate with the proximal phalanges of the digits. The heads form the knuckles on the dorsal surface of the hand when the fingers are flexed.

Gray’s Anatomy — Upper Limb: Hand & Wrist (Segment 11)

Carpal Bones（腕骨）

Carpal bones（腕骨） 包括：

  • Lunate（月骨）
  • Pisiform（豆骨）
  • Triquetrum（三角骨）
  • Trapezoid（大多角骨）
  • Tubercle of scaphoid（舟狀骨結節）
  • Scaphoid（舟狀骨）
  • Capitate（頭狀骨）

腕骨排列成** carpal arch（腕骨弓），遠端與metacarpals（掌骨）**相連。

Phalanges（指骨）

Phalanges（指骨） 是手指的骨骼：

  • Thumb（拇指）：兩節 — proximal phalanx（近節指骨） 和 distal phalanx（遠節指骨）
  • 其餘四指：各三節 — proximal phalanx（近節指骨）、middle phalanx（中節指骨）、distal phalanx（遠節指骨）

每節指骨包含：

  • Base（基底）：近端關節面
  • Shaft/Body（骨幹）
  • Head（頭部）：遠端

臨床重點：Distal phalanx（遠節指骨） 的頭部為非關節面，變平形成palmar tuberosity（掌側粗隆），位於指尖掌側墊下方。

Joints（關節）

Wrist Joint（腕關節）

Wrist joint（腕關節） 是滑膜關節，位於：

  • Radius（橈骨） 遠端
  • Articular disc（關節盤）：覆蓋ulna（尺骨） 遠端
  • Scaphoid（舟狀骨）、lunate（月骨）、triquetrum（三角骨）

腕骨關節面形成橢圓形凸面，與radius 和articular disc 的凹面吻合。

運動範圍：可做abduction（外展）、adduction（內收）、flexion（屈曲）、extension（伸展）。

臨床重點：由於radial styloid process（橈骨莖突） 比ulnar styloid process（尺骨莖突） 更遠端，手部向內收的角度大於向外展。

韌帶加強：

  • Palmar radiocarpal ligament（掌側橈腕韌帶）
  • Palmar ulnocarpal ligament（掌側尺腕韌帶）
  • Dorsal radiocarpal ligament（背側橈腕韌帶）
  • Radial collateral ligament（橈側副韌帶）
  • Ulnar collateral ligament（尺側副韌帶）

Carpal Joints（腕骨間關節）

** carpal joints（腕骨間關節）** 共享一個關節腔，活動度有限，但有助於abduction、adduction、flexion，尤其是extension。

Carpometacarpal Joints（腕掌關節）

五個** carpometacarpal joints（腕掌關節）** 連接metacarpals 與腕骨遠端列。

  • Thumb CMC joint（拇指腕掌關節）：為saddle joint（鞍狀關節），活動範圍最大，可做flexion、extension、abduction、adduction、rotation、circumduction
  • Metacarpals II–V 的 CMC joints：活動度較小，僅允許有限滑動，metacarpal V 滑動最大

Metacarpophalangeal Joints（掌指關節）

Metacarpophalangeal joints（掌指關節，MCP joints） 是condylar joints（髁狀關節），允許flexion、extension、abduction、adduction、circumduction、有限旋轉。

韌帶：

  • Palmar ligament（掌側韌帶）
  • Medial collateral ligament（內側副韌帶）
  • Lateral collateral ligament（外側副韌帶）

Deep Transverse Metacarpal Ligaments（掌側骨間韌帶）

三條deep transverse metacarpal ligaments（掌側骨間韌帶） 連接各手指MCP joint 的掌側韌帶。

臨床重點：Thumb（拇指） 的 MCP joint 掌側韌帶與index finger（食指） 的 MCP joint 掌側韌帶之間沒有深橫掌骨韌帶。此特點加上trapezo-metacarpal saddle joint（大多角骨-掌骨鞍狀關節），賦予拇指較大的活動度。

Interphalangeal Joints of Hand（手指指間關節）

Interphalangeal joints（指間關節，IP joints） 為hinge joints（樞軸關節），主要活動為flexion 和extension。

Carpal Tunnel（腕隧道）

Carpal tunnel（腕隧道） 前方由腕骨溝與flexor retinaculum（屈肌支持帶） 構成深弧形。

  • Medial border（內側界）：pisiform（豆骨）、hook of hamate（鉤骨鉤）
  • Lateral border（外側界）：scaphoid tubercle（舟狀骨結節）、tubercle of trapezium（大多角骨結節）

Contents of Carpal Tunnel（腕隧道內容物）

穿過腕隧道的結構：

  • 四條flexor digitorum profundus tendons（指深屈肌腱）
  • 四條flexor digitorum superficialis tendons（指淺屈肌腱）
  • Flexor pollicis longus tendon（拇指長屈肌腱）
  • Median nerve（正中神經）

臨床重點：Median nerve（正中神經） 位於腕隧道內肌腱的前方。

Structures NOT in Carpal Tunnel（腕隧道外結構）

不經過腕隧道的結構：

  • Flexor carpi radialis tendon（橈側屈腕肌腱）：有單獨滑膜鞘，通過trapezium tubercle（大多角骨結節） 溝槽
  • Ulnar artery（尺動脈）、ulnar nerve（尺神經）、palmaris longus tendon（掌長肌腱）：位於flexor retinaculum（屈肌支持帶） 前方
  • Radial artery（橈動脈）：繞過腕關節外側背面，鄰近scaphoid（舟狀骨）

Extensor Tendons at Wrist（腕部伸肌腱）

伸肌腱在腕關節六個間隔中通過，由extensor retinaculum（伸肌支持帶） 固定：

間隔 內容物 位置
1 Abductor pollicis longus、extensor pollicis brevis tendons 外側
2 Extensor carpi radialis longus、extensor carpi radialis brevis tendons 外側
3 Extensor pollicis longus tendon 外側
4 Extensor digitorum、extensor indicis tendons 背面
5 Extensor digiti minimi tendon 內側
6 Extensor carpi ulnaris tendon 內側

Palmar Aponeurosis（掌腱膜）

Palmar aponeurosis（掌腱膜） 是覆蓋手掌的深筋膜三角形濃縮結構。

  • Apex（頂點）：與palmaris longus tendon（掌長肌腱） 連續；若無此肌腱，則附著於flexor retinaculum（屈肌支持帶）
  • Fibers（纖維）：放射狀延伸至各指的根部

臨床重點：血管、神經和長屈肌腱位於掌腱膜深層。

Palmaris Brevis（掌短肌）

Palmaris brevis（掌短肌） 是覆蓋hypothenar muscles（小魚際肌）、ulnar artery（尺動脈）、ulnar nerve淺支的小塊皮下肌肉。

  • Origin（起點）：掌腱膜、屈肌支持帶
  • Insertion（止點）：手掌內側緣皮膚真皮
  • Function（功能）：收縮加深掌心弧度、改善握力
  • Innervation（神經支配）：Ulnar nerve 淺支

Anatomical Snuffbox（鼻煙窩）

Anatomical snuffbox（鼻煙窩） 是腕關節背面外側的三角形凹陷。

Boundaries（邊界）

  • Lateral border（外側界）：abductor pollicis longus、extensor pollicis brevis 肌腱
  • Medial border（內側界）：extensor pollicis longus 肌腱
  • Floor（底部）：scaphoid（舟狀骨）、trapezium（大多角骨）、extensor carpi radialis longus、extensor carpi radialis brevis 肌腱遠端

Contents（內容物）

  • Radial artery（橈動脈）：斜向穿過，位於伸拇指肌腱深層，鄰近scaphoid 和trapezium
  • Superficial branch of radial nerve（橈神經淺支） 終末部分
  • Cephalic vein（頭靜脈） 起點（來自手背靜脈弓）

臨床重點：當手向尺側偏斜時，scaphoid（舟狀骨） 可在鼻煙窩內觸及。此位置可用於評估骨折。Radial artery（橈動脈） 脈搏也可在窩內觸摸。

Fibrous Digital Sheaths（纖維性指鞘）

屈肌腱離開腕隧道後，進入手指掌側的fibrous sheaths（纖維鞘）。

特點

  • 近端起於metacarpophalangeal joint（掌指關節） 前方，延伸至distal phalanges（遠節指骨）
  • 由fibrous arches（纖維弓） 和 cruciate ligaments（十字韌帶） 構成
  • 功能：將肌腱固定於骨面，防止屈曲時肌腱「弓起」

每個鞘內有synovial sheath（滑膜鞘） 包繞肌腱。拇指和little finger（小指） 的滑膜鞘與腕隧道內的滑膜鞘相延續。

Extensor Hoods（伸肌腱帽）

Extensor hoods（伸肌腱帽） 又稱dorsal digital expansions（背側指伸裝置），由伸肌腱在近節指骨背側擴展形成。

結構

每個伸肌腱帽為三角形：

  • Apex（尖）：附著於distal phalanx（遠節指骨）
  • Central region（中央區）：附著於middle phalanx（中節指骨）（示指、中指、環指、小指）或 proximal phalanx（近節指骨）（拇指）
  • Base corners（底角）：繞過MCP joint 兩側

附著肌肉

  • Index、middle、ring、little fingers：lumbricals（小魚際肌）、interossei（骨間肌）、abductor digiti minimi
  • Thumb：adductor pollicis（拇指內收肌）、abductor pollicis brevis（拇指外展肌短肌）

臨床重點：由於這些小肌肉的力量施加在 MCP joint 支點的遠端，它們屈曲 MCP joint，同時通過伸肌腱帽將力量傳至背側，伸展 IP joints（指間關節）。這種能力使我們能屈曲掌指關節同時伸展指間關節——例如寫字時「t」的上挑。

Intrinsic Muscles of Hand（手部固有肌）

Interossei（骨間肌）

骨間肌位於metacarpals（掌骨） 之間，附著於相鄰掌骨，插入各指proximal phalanx（近節指骨） 和extensor hood（伸肌腱帽）。

Dorsal Interossei（背側骨間肌）

四塊背側骨間肌，作用為**abduction（外展）**手指。

Palmar Interossei（掌側骨間肌）

三塊掌側骨間肌，作用為**adduction（內收）**手指。

臨床重點：第一掌側骨間肌若存在，常被視為adductor pollicis（拇指內收肌） 或 flexor pollicis brevis（拇指短屈肌） 的一部分。

Adductor Pollicis（拇指內收肌）

Adductor pollicis（拇指內收肌） 有兩個頭：

  • Transverse head（橫頭）

  • Oblique head（斜頭）

  • Origin（起點）：橫頭起於第三掌骨掌側面；斜頭起於腕骨

  • Insertion（止點）：拇指proximal phalanx（近節指骨）、sesamoid bones（籽骨）

  • Function（功能）：內收拇指

  • Innervation（神經支配）：Deep branch of ulnar nerve（尺神經深支）

Thenar Muscles（大魚際肌）

Thenar muscles（大魚際肌） 構成手掌外側拇指根部。

肌肉 英文 起點 止點 功能 神經支配
Abductor pollicis brevis 拇指外展短肌 Trapezium、flexor retinaculum 拇指近節指骨 外展 Median nerve
Flexor pollicis brevis 拇指屈曲短肌 Trapezium、flexor retinaculum 拇指近節指骨、籽骨 屈曲 Median nerve
Opponens pollicis 拇指對掌肌 Trapezium、flexor retinaculum 拇指掌骨外側 對掌 Median nerve

Hypothenar Muscles（小魚際肌）

Hypothenar muscles（小魚際肌） 構成手掌內側小指根部。

肌肉 英文 起點 止點 功能 神經支配
Abductor digiti minimi 小指外展肌 Pisiform、豆骨鉤 小指近節指骨 外展 Ulnar nerve
Flexor digiti minimi brevis 小指屈曲短肌 Hook of hamate、flexor retinaculum 小指近節指骨 屈曲 Ulnar nerve
Opponens digiti minimi 小指對掌肌 Hook of hamate、flexor retinaculum 小指掌骨內側 對掌 Ulnar nerve

Lumbricals（蚓狀肌）

四塊lumbricals（蚓狀肌） 起於flexor digitorum profundus tendons（指深屈肌腱），止於extensor hoods（伸肌腱帽）。

  • 第一、第二蚓狀肌（外側兩塊）：Median nerve（正中神經）
  • 第三、第四蚓狀肌（內側兩塊）：Ulnar nerve（尺神經）

臨床重點：手部固有肌的神經支配幾乎全部來自Ulnar nerve 深支（支配所有骨間肌、蚓狀肌、內收肌、大部分小魚際肌），除了三塊大魚際肌和兩塊外側蚓狀肌由Median nerve（正中神經） 支配。脊髓節段主要為 T1，有 C8 的補充。

臨床摘要

Scaphoid Fracture & Avascular Necrosis（舟狀骨骨折與缺血性壞死）

臨床重點：最常見的腕骨損傷是舟狀骨腰部骨折。約 10% 的個案，scaphoid（舟狀骨） 的唯一血供來自radial artery（橈動脈），由骨頭遠端進入供應近端。當腰部骨折發生時，近端可能發生avascular necrosis（缺血性壞死）。無法預測哪些患者有此血供特徵。

Carpal Tunnel Syndrome（腕隧道症候群）

臨床重點：腕隧道症候群是正中神經在腕隧道內受壓迫的嵌壓症候群。常見病因包括：過度使用、肌腱及腱鞘腫脹（如類風濕性關節炎）、腕關節囊腫。發病機制：腕隧道內壓力增加 → 靜脈充血 → 神經水腫 → 毛細血管內皮缺氧損傷。

症狀：

  • 疼痛、感覺異常（螞蟻爬行感）分布於正中神經支配區
  • 大魚際肌無力、肌肉萎縮

檢查：輕叩屈肌支持帶區域的正中神經可誘發症狀（Tinel’s sign）。

治療：

  • 初期：消炎、去除誘因
  • 若無改善：神經傳導檢查確認，必要時手術切開flexor retinaculum（屈肌支持帶） 減壓

De Quervain’s Syndrome（德奎爾文氏症候群）

臨床重點：De Quervain’s syndrome 是第一背側伸肌間隔的炎症性疾病，影響extensor pollicis brevis tendon（伸拇指短肌腱） 和 abductor pollicis longus tendon（拇指外展長肌腱） 及其共同腱鞘。

典型表現：嚴重腕痛，影響拇指屈伸及外展。常見於過度使用者，如需經常抱小孩的年輕母親。其他病因包括類風濕性關節炎等炎症性疾病。

Tenosynovitis（腱鞘炎）

臨床重點：腱鞘炎是肌腱及其腱鞘的炎症，可由過度使用引起，也與類風濕性關節炎、結締組織疾病相關。嚴重時纖維化導致肌腱在鞘內黏滯，活動時需過度用力，產生「扳機」現象。

Trigger Finger（扳機指）

臨床重點：扳機指是兒童和成人的常見疾病，特徵為屈肌腱在手中卡住或彈響，偶爾鎖定。常與功能障礙和疼痛相關。病因主要是掌側纖維鞘在掌指關節水平的纖維化和緊縮。

Gray’s Anatomy — Upper Limb: Hand (Segment 12)

Dorsal Interossei（背側骨間肌）

Dorsal interossei 是所有內在肌中位置最背側的肌肉，可透過手背皮膚觸摸感知（圖 7.100）。共有 四塊雙羽狀（bipennate）Dorsal interosseous muscles，位於相鄰的 metacarpal bones（掌骨）之間（圖 7.100）。

每塊肌肉同時附著於：

  • **Proximal phalanx（近節指骨）**的底部
  • 相應手指的 extensor hood（伸肌裝置）

附著細節

肌肉 附著側
第二 Dorsal interosseous **Middle finger（中指）**的外側
第三 Dorsal interosseous Middle finger 的內側
第四 Dorsal interosseous **Ring finger（無名指）**的內側
第一 Dorsal interosseous（最大） **Index finger（食指）**的外側

功能

除了透過伸肌裝置產生手指的 **屈曲（flexion）**與 伸展（extension） 動作外，Dorsal interossei 是 index、middle、ring fingers 在 **metacarpophalangeal joints（掌指關節）**處的主要 外展肌（abductors）。

臨床重點：Thumb 與 little finger 各自有自己的外展肌，因此沒有 dorsal interossei。Thumb 的外展由 abductor pollicis brevis 負責，little finger 的外展由 abductor digiti minimi 負責。

臨床重點：**Radial artery（橈動脈）**在穿過 **anatomical snuffbox（鼻煙窩）**後，進入手掌深層前，會穿過 第一 Dorsal interosseous muscle 的兩個頭之間。

Palmar Interossei（掌側骨間肌）

Palmar interossei 有三塊（或四塊），位於 dorsal interossei 的前方，為 **單羽狀（unipennate）**肌肉，各自起於相應手指的 metacarpals（圖 7.101）。

各塊附著

肌肉 起點 止點
第一 Palmar interosseous Metacarpal I 掌側面的內側 Thumb 的 proximal phalanx 底部及 extensor hood
第二 Palmar interosseous Metacarpal II 的內側面 Index finger extensor hood 的內側
第三 Palmar interosseous Metacarpal IV 的外側面 Ring finger extensor hood 的外側
第四 Palmar interosseous Metacarpal V 的外側面 Little finger extensor hood 的外側

臨床重點：第一 Palmar interosseous muscle 時常退化臨床上常被視為 adductor pollicis 或 flexor pollicis brevis 的一部分。其肌腱中常見 sesamoid bone（籽骨）。

Palmar interossei 的功能是使 thumb、index、ring、little fingers 相對於通過 middle finger 的長軸做 內收（adduction），動作發生在 metacarpophalangeal joints。

Adductor Pollicis（拇指內收肌）

Adductor pollicis 是一塊大型三角形肌肉，位於骨間肌前方，橫跨手掌（圖 7.102）。

起點（兩個頭）

  • Transverse head（橫頭）：來自 Metacarpal III 骨幹的掌側面
  • Oblique head（斜頭）：來自 **Capitate（頭狀骨）**及相鄰的 Metacarpals II、III 的底部

止點

兩個頭會合形成肌腱（常含 sesamoid bone），附著於：

  • Thumb proximal phalanx 底部的內側
  • Extensor hood

臨床重點：Radial artery 在兩頭之間向前內側走，穿過手掌深層形成 deep palmar arch（掌深弓）。

Adductor pollicis 是強力的 拇指內收肌，在抓握時使拇指與其他手指相對（對掌運動）。

Thenar Muscles（魚際肌群）

Thenar muscles 包括三塊肌肉（圖 7.103），負責拇指的 **對掌（opposition）**及精細動作，構成手掌外側、拇指基部的明顯隆起（thenar eminence）。

所有 Thenar muscles 均由 **median nerve（正中神經）**的 **recurrent branch（返支）**支配。

Opponens Pollicis（拇指對掌肌）

  • 起點：**Trapezium（大多角骨）**的結節及相鄰的 flexor retinaculum（屈肌支持帶）
  • 止點：Metacarpal I 整個外側緣及相鄰的掌側面
  • 功能：在 trapezium 上旋轉並屈曲 metacarpal I，使拇指墊面向手指墊

Abductor Pollicis Brevis（拇指短展肌）

  • 起點：**Scaphoid（舟狀骨）**和 trapezium 的結節及相鄰的 flexor retinaculum
  • 止點：Thumb proximal phalanx 底部外側及 extensor hood
  • 功能：在 metacarpophalangeal joint 處外展拇指

Flexor Pollicis Brevis（拇指短屈肌）

  • 起點：主要來自 trapezium 結節及相鄰的 flexor retinaculum；亦可能有較深層的附著
  • 止點：Thumb proximal phalanx 底部外側
  • 功能：屈曲拇指的 metacarpophalangeal joint
  • 備註：肌腱中常含 sesamoid bone

Hypothenar Muscles（小魚際肌群）

Hypothenar muscles 包括三塊肌肉（圖 7.103），構成手掌內側、小指基部的隆起（hypothenar eminence）。

與 thenar muscles 不同，hypothenar muscles 由 **ulnar nerve（尺神經）**的 deep branch 支配，而非 median nerve 的返支。

Opponens Digiti Minimi（小指對掌肌）

  • 起點：**Hamate（鉤骨）**的鉤突及相鄰的 flexor retinaculum
  • 止點：Metacarpal V 的內側緣及掌側面
  • 功能：將 Metacarpal V 旋轉向手掌

Abductor Digiti Minimi（小指展肌）

  • 起點：Pisiform（豌豆骨）、pisohamate ligament 及 flexor carpi ulnaris 的肌腱
  • 止點：Little finger proximal phalanx 底部內側及 extensor hood
  • 功能：小指的主要外展肌

Flexor Digiti Minimi Brevis（小指短屈肌）

  • 起點：Hamate 鉤突及相鄰的 flexor retinaculum
  • 止點：與 abductor digiti minimi 共同附著於 little finger proximal phalanx 底部內側
  • 功能：屈曲小指的 metacarpophalangeal joint

Lumbrical Muscles（蚓狀肌）

共有 四塊 Lumbrical muscles，各與一根手指相連。肌肉起於 **flexor digitorum profundus（指深屈肌）**在手掌中的肌腱。

肌肉 形態 起點
Medial two（第二、三） 雙羽狀（bipennate） 分別來自 middle + ring finger 及 ring + little finger 的 FDP tendons
Lateral two（第一、四） 單羽狀（unipennate） 分別來自 index 及 middle finger 的 FDP tendons

Lumbricals 繞過手指外側向背側走行，附著於 extensor hood（圖 7.104）。

臨床重點：Lumbricals 獨特之處在於連接 屈肌腱 與 伸肌腱。透過附著於 extensor hood，它們參與屈曲 metacarpophalangeal joints 並伸展 interphalangeal joints。

神經支配

肌肉 神經支配
Medial two lumbricals Ulnar nerve 的 deep branch
Lateral two lumbricals Median nerve 的 digital branches

表格：手部內在肌總覽

肌肉 起點 止點 神經支配 功能

Dorsal interossei（四塊） 相鄰 metacarpals Extensor hood、proximal phalanges Deep branch of ulnar nerve（C8, T1） Index、middle、ring fingers 在 MCP joint 的外展
Palmar interossei（三或四塊） 各手指的 metacarpals Thumb、index、ring、little fingers 的 extensor hoods Deep branch of ulnar nerve（C8, T1） Thumb、index、ring、little fingers 在 MCP joint 的內收
Adductor pollicis Transverse head: Metacarpal III；Oblique head: Capitate、Metacarpals II、III Proximal phalanx of thumb、extensor hood Deep branch of ulnar nerve（C8, T1） 拇指內收
Lumbricals（四塊） Flexor digitorum profundus tendons Extensor hoods Medial two: ulnar nerve；Lateral two: median nerve 屈曲 MCP joints、伸展 IP joints
